title: Emergency Department Waiting Time, Communication, and Patient Perceptions of Care: A Cross- Sectional Study in a Lebanese Hospital
abstract: Abstract Background Emergency department (ED) waiting time is an important component of patient experience and may influence perceptions of care quality and satisfaction. This study aimed to examine the associations between perceived ED waiting time, communication regarding expected waiting times, and patients’ perceptions of care, satisfaction, and waiting-related concerns in a Lebanese hospital. Methods An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted among 288 conscious, clinically stable, non-critical patients attending the emergency department of Haykel Hospital, Lebanon. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing perceived waiting time, communication regarding expected waiting times, perceived effects of waiting on satisfaction and care, complaint-related concerns, awareness of the right to refuse care because of unacceptable waiting time, and suggested improvement strategies. Descriptive statistics, Spearman’s rank correlation, and binary logistic regression were performed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 27.0.1. Results Among participants, 146 (50.7%) reported receiving information regarding the expected waiting time. Patients who were informed about the expected waiting time reported more favorable waiting-time perceptions in the unadjusted analysis. title: Survival and clinical outcomes of critically ill COVID-19 patients requiring invasive mechanical ventilation in Palestine: A multicenter retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Critically ill patients with COVID-19 often require invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), which is associated with increased fatality rates. There is a lack of data on survival and outcomes in resource-limited settings such as Palestine. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the survival rate and clinical outcomes of COVID-19 patients requiring invasive mechanical ventilation in Palestinian intensive care units (ICUs) and to explore clinical factors associated with mortality in this critically ill cohort. We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study of all adult COVID-19 patients requiring invasive mechanical ventilation and hospitalized in the intensive care units (ICUs) of three prominent Palestinian hospitals from August 1, 2020, to April 30, 2021. We rigorously extracted comprehensive data on demographic, clinical, laboratory, treatment, and outcome characteristics from patients' medical records. Of the 150 patients necessitating invasive mechanical ventilation, only 13 (8.7%) survived to hospital discharge. Younger age was associated with survival in univariable analysis (OR = 0.948, p = 0.006). Coronary artery disease was more frequent among non-survivors (p = 0.041), and peak creatinine levels were significantly higher among non-survivors (p = 0.008). In univariable analysis, pressure-control ventilation mode (OR = 4.416, p = 0.022), lower minimum FiO2 (OR = 0.883, p = 0.001), and lower minimum inspiratory pressure (OR = 0.478, p = 0.010) were associated with survival. These results should be interpreted with caution, as they most likely reflect variations in disease severity and underlying lung mechanics rather than a direct effect of the ventilation mode. Remdesivir use was associated with higher odds of survival in univariable analysis (OR = 5.783, p = 0.004). The median duration of invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) was 15 days for survivors compared to 6 days for non-survivors (p < 0.001). Survivors had a longer IMV duration, reflecting a prolonged clinical course rather than a causal effect. The median length of stay in the intensive care unit (ICU) was 27 days for survivors versus 11 days for non-survivors. Acute kidney injury (60.7%) and cardiovascular complications (45.3%) were associated with worse outcomes. Tracheostomy was more frequently observed among survivors in univariable analysis. Morbid obesity was associated with survival in univariable analysis. The survival rate among critically ill COVID-19 patients requiring invasive mechanical ventilation in Palestine was very low. Survival was associated with younger age and lower peak creatinine levels, while acute kidney injury and cardiovascular complications were associated with worse outcomes. Given the retrospective design and small number of survivors, these associations should be interpreted as exploratory rather than independent predictors of survival. These findings highlight the challenges of managing critically ill patients during a pandemic in a resource-constrained healthcare system and the importance of strengthening critical care capacity and preparedness for future health emergencies.

title: Early clinical judgment in adult autism referrals: association with diagnostic outcome, verification bias and equity in an NHS triage pathway
Corruption in health systems: An umbrella review of the pathways to health, financial, and social outcomes.
abstract: Corruption in health systems is increasingly perceived to undermine governance, equity, and service delivery, posing a major barrier to achieving universal health coverage and the Sustainable Development Goals. To fill the evidence gap, this umbrella review synthesises findings from twelve systematic reviews and meta-analyses to examine how health-sector corruption affects health, financial, and social outcomes. It identifies common types of corruption, including substandard and falsified medicines (SFM), informal payments, absenteeism, pharmaceutical promotion, procurement fraud, and billing abuse, and maps the pathways by which they affect outcomes. The review reveals two recurring dynamics: incentives arising from systemic vulnerabilities and opportunities created by governance failures. SFM contribute to avoidable mortality and economic strain, particularly in low-resource settings. Informal payments and absenteeism disproportionately affect poor and rural populations, eroding trust and deepening inequities. The pharmaceutical industry's influence distorts prescribing practices, raising costs and compromising care quality. Findings suggest that isolated interventions are insufficient. Effective anti-corruption strategies must reduce incentives through fair pay and adequate resources, close off opportunities via digitalisation and process reform, and strengthen accountability through independent oversight and transparency. The review also underscores the need for improved economic modelling and data quality to quantify the burden of corruption better. Despite limitations, including reliance on secondary sources and heterogeneity across studies, this synthesis provides a system-level framework for understanding corruption's impact and guiding targeted, context-sensitive reforms. It contributes to the Lancet Global Health Commission on Anti-Corruption in Health's efforts to advance transparency, accountability, and health equity.

Tetanus Burden in a Ghanaian Tertiary Care Setting: A Retrospective Analysis of Clinical Presentations, Management, and Mortality Predictors (2020-2024)
abstract: Abstract Background Tetanus remains a significant cause of morbidity and mortality in low- and middle-income countries despite being entirely preventable through vaccination. In Ghana, the last comprehensive study of adult tetanus outcomes was conducted two decades ago, and it is unknown whether outcomes have improved amid expanded vaccination programs, evolving wound care, and the establishment of emergency medicine as a recognised specialty. This study aimed to describe the demographic, clinical, and management characteristics of adult tetanus patients at a tertiary referral centre, determine the case fatality rate, and identify independent predictors of mortality. Methods A retrospective, single-centre study was conducted at the Emergency Department of Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital in Kumasi, Ghana, among patients aged 15 years and older with a clinical diagnosis of tetanus admitted between August 2020 and August 2024. Data were extracted from electronic medical records using a standardised form and analysed with Stata version 14. Bivariate associations were assessed using Chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, and Firth's penalised likelihood logistic regression was used for multivariable analysis given the small sample size. Results Forty-seven patients were admitted with tetanus during the study period. The median age was 42.9 years, and 91.5% were male. Nail puncture was the predominant injury (40.4%), and 17.0% had no recorded portal of entry. The overall case fatality rate was 51.1%, with substantial year-to-year fluctuation (28.6% in 2020 to 75% in 2022). Independent predictors of mortality included management entirely in the emergency department without ward transfer (AOR = 25.2), hospital stay of ≤ 7 days (AOR = 65.2), and intubation (AOR = 23.0); all eight intubated patients died. Tetanus immunoglobulin was administered to 74.5% of patients, and 25.5% received none. Conclusion Adult tetanus mortality in Ghana has not improved in two decades, remaining at approximately 51%. These outcomes reflect a failure of health-system configuration rather than clinical knowledge, with the absence of dedicated critical care capacity driving the universal fatality among intubated patients. Protocolized care pathways with designated high-dependency capacity and reliable post-exposure prophylaxis are urgently needed.

Prognostic Association and Incremental Predictive Value of NT-proBNP in Emergency Department Patients With Sepsis
abstract: Background N-terminal pro–B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) is frequently elevated in sepsis and may reflect cardiac stress, cardiorenal dysfunction, and acute illness severity. However, its adjusted prognostic association and incremental predictive value beyond routinely available clinical information in emergency department (ED) patients with sepsis remain uncertain. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults admitted through the emergency department with suspected infection between November 1, 2018, and February 28, 2026, who met Sepsis-3 criteria and had an eligible NT-proBNP measurement within 24 hours after hospital admission. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. NT-proBNP concentrations were log2-transformed, and odds ratios (ORs) represented associations per doubling of NT-proBNP concentration. Logistic regression models were sequentially adjusted for demographic characteristics, comorbidities, and Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score. Quartile-based analyses, tests for trend, restricted cubic spline analyses, and sensitivity analyses were performed. Incremental predictive value was assessed by comparing a prespecified base clinical model with an NT-proBNP–extended model using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), Brier score, calibration measures, bootstrap internal validation, and decision curve analysis. Results Among 2,994 included patients, 567 died during hospitalization (18.9%). The median NT-proBNP concentration was 1,382 pg/mL (interquartile range, 391–5,133 pg/mL), and the median interval from hospital admission to NT-proBNP measurement was 4.0 hours (interquartile range, 2.0–8.0 hours). In the primary adjusted model, each doubling of NT-proBNP was associated with higher odds of in-hospital mortality (OR, 1.074; 95% CI, 1.027–1.123; P = 0.002). Compared with the lowest NT-proBNP quartile, the highest quartile was associated with higher mortality odds (OR, 1.653; 95% CI, 1.204–2.275; P = 0.002; P for trend = 0.003). Restricted cubic spline analysis showed an overall association (P = 0.014) without evidence of nonlinearity (P = 0.487). Findings were directionally consistent in timing-restricted analyses, after exclusion of values at the assay reporting boundary, and when NEWS replaced SOFA. The base clinical model had an apparent AUC of 0.705 (95% CI, 0.681–0.728), compared with 0.710 (95% CI, 0.687–0.733) after addition of NT-proBNP (ΔAUC, 0.0050; 95% CI, −0.0002 to 0.0102; P = 0.059). The apparent Brier score decreased from 0.1410 to 0.1407 (ΔBrier, −0.0003); after bootstrap optimism correction, the AUC difference was 0.0045 and the Brier-score difference was −0.0001. Calibration was similar between models. The NT-proBNP–extended model showed small and nonuniform apparent net-benefit differences across decision thresholds. Conclusions Higher NT-proBNP concentrations were associated with in-hospital mortality after adjustment for measured clinical factors, but added little to prediction beyond routinely available information. These findings do not support routine use of NT-proBNP for mortality risk stratification in unselected ED patients with sepsis.

title: Combined inflammatory and metabolic biomarkers predict the mortality rate of patients with acute dyspnoea
abstract: Objective To investigate whether plasma concentrations of inflammatory biomarkers and amino acids in patients presenting to the emergency department with acute dyspnoea predict 90-day mortality. Background Acute dyspnoea is a common reason for emergency department (ED) visits and has heterogeneous causes; rapid risk stratification is essential. Biomarkers may complement clinical assessment. We previously found that interleukin-8 (IL-8), growth differentiation factor-15 (GDF-15), and the amino acids glycine, phenylalanine and valine were independently associated with 90-day mortality in acute dyspnoea. Methods Inflammatory biomarkers and amino acids were analysed in adults admitted to the ED at Skane University Hospital, Malmo, Sweden (2013–2016), and 90-day mortality was modelled using Cox proportional hazards adjusted for age, sex, oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, C-reactive protein (CRP), estimated glomerular filtration (eGFR), lactate and the “Medical Emergency Triage and Treatment System-Adult” score. The inflammatory biomarker score (IL-8 and GDF-15) was replicated in 448 newly collected patients. The combined effect of the amino acid mortality risk score (AMRS) and the inflammatory biomarker mortality risk score (IBMRS) was tested in 637 patients, assessing discrimination (AUC), risk reclassification (Net Reclassification Improvement), and internal validation by bootstrap resampling. Results In the replication cohort (n=448): 57 patients (12.7%) died within 90 days. Mortality was 1.8% in quartile 1 vs 28.6% in quartile 4 of the inflammatory biomarker score; per 1 SD increment, hazard ratio was 2.01 (95% CI 1.44–2.81) after multivariable adjustment. In the combined cohort (n=637): 90-day mortality was 12.2% (n=78), with 1.2% mortality in quartile 1 and 32% in quartile 4. After multivariable adjustment, hazard ratio was 2.83 (95% CI 2.12–3.77) per 1 SD increment and was thirteen times greater for Q4 than for Q1. Adding the combined biomarker risk score to standard clinical predictors increased the time-dependent AUC from 0.79 (95% CI 0.74–0.84) to 0.85 (95% CI 0.82–0.89); the optimism-corrected Harrell’s C-index was 0.81 and the calibration slope was 0.88. Conclusion Independent associations between IL-8 and GDF-15 and 90-day mortality in acute dyspnoea were replicated. IL-8, GDF-15, glycine, valine, and phenylalanine independently predicted 90-day mortality, improving AUC by approximately seven percentage points.

title: Perioperative Relative Albumin Decline and Post-sampling Remaining Length of Stay After Lung Resection: Findings From the INSPIRE Cohort and an Independent Hospital Cohort
abstract: Objectives Early postoperative albumin decline may reflect the physiological response to lung resection and provide information beyond the preoperative albumin level. We investigated its association with remaining hospital stay and assessed the consistency of this association in an independent hospital cohort. Methods This retrospective cohort study used the INSPIRE perioperative database and an independent cohort of lung resection procedures performed at the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University between December 2023 and June 2024. Relative albumin decline was calculated from the preoperative and early postoperative measurements. The primary outcome was the interval from postoperative albumin sampling to hospital discharge. In INSPIRE, log-transformed remaining hospital stay was analysed using multivariable linear regression with a 3-degree-of-freedom natural spline for preoperative albumin and HC3 robust standard errors. The hospital cohort underwent additional adjustment for operative characteristics, comorbidities, pulmonary function and intraoperative blood loss. Results Among 3,568 patients in INSPIRE, 3,323 had paired albumin measurements and were included in the primary analysis. Each 10-percentage-point increase in relative albumin decline was associated with a 6.34% longer remaining hospital stay (95% confidence interval [CI], 3.34–9.43; P < 0.001). The association persisted after excluding stays longer than 30 days (3.99%; 95% CI, 1.36–6.70) and in inverse probability-weighted analysis (6.22%; 95% CI, 3.20–9.32). In the hospital cohort, the fully adjusted common-sample analysis of 792 procedures showed a corresponding increase of 3.59% (95% CI, 1.28–5.95; P = 0.002). Conclusions Greater early perioperative relative albumin decline was associated with longer remaining hospital stay after lung resection. This association was consistent across the INSPIRE and independent hospital cohorts. Early albumin change may provide complementary information on postoperative recovery, although its clinical utility requires prospective evaluation.

title: Kikuchi–fujimoto disease presenting as acute appendicitis-like manifestations in children: a case series of eight patients
abstract: Objective To summarize the clinical characteristics of pediatric Kikuchi–Fujimoto disease (KFD) presenting with acute appendicitis-like manifestations. Methods We retrospectively analyzed the clinical data of children with KFD who presented with acute appendicitis-like manifestations admitted from January 2018 to January 2026, summarizing their clinical manifestations, laboratory findings, imaging ﬁndings, and treatment protocols. Results Eight patients aged 6–14 years (median, 10 years; 6 boys and 2 girls) were included. All presented with fever (median duration, 13.5 days; IQR, 9–23.5) and abdominal pain, whlie McBurney point tenderness was noted in 5/8 patients (62.5%). Leukocyte counts were low-normal or decreased in all patients (median, 3.6 × 10 9 /L; IQR, 2.25–4.20 × 10 9 /L), and procalcitonin levels were extremely low (<0.2 ng/mL) in all. Elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate were each observed in 4/8 patients (50%). Only two patients (25%) had transaminase elevation. Ultrasonography detected cervical lymphadenopathy in 7/8 patients (87.5%) and abdominal lymphadenopathy in 6/8 (75.0%), most commonly in the right lower quadrant mesentery and ileocecal region. Appendiceal enlargement (increased outer diameter) was observed in 7 of the 8 patients (87.5%), with a median maximum diameter of 6.8 mm (IQR, 6.6–9.0 mm). Lymph node biopsy was performed in all eight patients and showed histopathological changes compatible with histiocytic necrotizing lymphadenitis. All eight patients received antibiotics, and four (50%) received glucocorticoids and conservative management with serial appendiceal ultrasonography at 5–7day intervals. Appendectomy was performed in three patients (P5, P7, and P8), revealing subacute appendicitis in two and acute suppurative necrotizing appendicitis in one. All patients improved and were discharged after a median hospitalization of 11 days (IQR, 8.5–16.5), and all completed 1-year follow-up. One patient developed undifferentiated connective tissue disease 6 months after discharge, and no appendiceal inflammation recurred in patients who did not undergo appendectomy. Conclusion Pediatric KFD presenting initially with fever, abdominal pain, and McBurney point tenderness is rare and frequently misdiagnosed. Although superficial lymphadenopathy, leukopenia, normal or low PCT levels, and mild widening of the appendiceal outer diameter may support a diagnosis of KFD in the appropriate clinical context, these features are nonspecific and do not exclude progression to true appendicitis. Serial monitoring of disease activity and regular follow-up ultrasonography of the appendix are therefore recommended to avoid missing true appendicitis.

title: Assessing lymphatic drainage of the colon and rectum by single-photon emission computerised tomography: a feasibility study in patients undergoing standard-of-care colonoscopy
abstract: Objective The splenic flexure (SF) has variable lymphatic drainage due to its heterogeneous vascular supply, contributing to uncertainty regarding optimal oncological resection. This study evaluated the feasibility and safety of in vivo lymphatic mapping of the SF and rectum using endoscopic submucosal Technetium-99 m (Tc-99 m) radiocolloid injection followed by planar lymphoscintigraphy and single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), and assessed the reproducibility of identifying a dominant lymphatic pedicle (DLP) consistently. Methods A prospective pilot study was conducted at Concord Repatriation General Hospital, Sydney (2022–2023), in patients undergoing standard-of-care colonoscopy who had macroscopically normal colorectal anatomy. Submucosal radiocolloid injections were administered at the SF (n = 10), upper rectum (n = 5) or lower rectum with direct digital massage (n = 5). Tc-99 m Nanoscan or Tc-99 m antimony trisulfide (40MBq in 1.3 mL, with methylene blue) was used. Serial planar lymphoscintigraphy was performed at 1, 2, 4 and 24 h, with SPECT at 1, 2 and 4 h and additional delayed imaging at 24 and/or 48 h. Imaging was assessed for tracer dispersion, nodal uptake and DLP identification. Results Submucosal injection was technically successful in all 20 patients, without extravasation or adverse events occurred at 1-, 7-, or 30-day follow-up. No consistent DLP was demonstrated following SF injections on planar or SPECT imaging, including on delayed imaging. Specifically, eight SF patients showed only focal or dispersed tracer activity and only two showed a DLP (i.e., inferior mesenteric artery [IMA]). Similarly, no lymphatic drainage or nodal uptake was demonstrated in any of the five upper rectal patients intended to be ‘positive controls’. In contrast, all patients who underwent lower rectal injections demonstrated lymphatic drainage following direct finger massage; with a DLP identified in three patients (60%), and LN activity observed in all five patients (100%) involving pelvic sidewall, presacral, iliac, and para-aortic regions. SPECT improved anatomical localisation compared with planar imaging alone. Conclusions Submucosal Tc-99 m radiocolloid injection combined with planar lymphoscintigraphy and SPECT is technically feasible and safe for colorectal lymphatic mapping. However, the current protocol does not reliably identify a DLP, even within the anatomically more predictable upper rectum, thereby limiting its immediate clinical applicability. Further technical refinement and independent validation are required before this approach can be considered suitable for routine preoperative colorectal lymphatic mapping. Trial registration Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ANZCTR) ID – ACTRN12622001439730 (Date of Registration: 10/11/2022); Therapeutic Goods Administration Clinical Trial Notification (TGA CTN) ID:7FX9YJ99.

title: AN INTEGRATED CAUSAL-PREDICTIVE OPTIMIZATION FRAMEWORK FOR HEALTHCARE RESOURCE EFFICIENCY, FINANCIAL RESILIENCE, AND SUSTAINABLE SERVICE DELIVERY
abstract: Hospitals must preserve surge capacity while meeting operating budgets, yet policy effects, workload forecasts, and allocation decisions require different kinds of evidence. This study develops an integrated framework and evaluates it using the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Hospital Provider Cost Report, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services hospital capacity records, and Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality national utilization estimates. The analytic panel contained 35,062 fiscal-year reports from 4,760 short-term and critical access hospitals for 2017–2024. A state-level difference-in-differences analysis compared the 2021 Medicaid expansions in Oklahoma and Missouri with eight comparison states. Relative to the comparison states, the treated states recorded a 3.99 percentage-point increase in the Medicaid inpatient-day share and a 3.20 percentage-point decline in operating margin. Reference probabilities from 45 state-pair reassignments were .089 and .289, respectively, leaving the margin effect uncertain. In a 2024 holdout of 4,155 hospitals, ridge regression achieved a mean absolute error of 2,493 annualized patient-days, compared with 2,638 for persistence. The paired state-bootstrap interval for the difference was −245 to −43 patient-days. Under an illustrative 3% reserve budget and an 80% planning threshold, scenario-based allocation reduced the modeled capacity gap from 3.26 million to 1.79 million bed-days, a 45.2% reduction under equal reserve budgets. The estimated capacity gains are retrospective model outputs. Realized savings, care access and clinical outcomes require prospective evaluation.

title: Morbidity and mortality in colorectal cancer according to the level of care at the beginning of the diagnostic process
abstract: Background: Colorectal cancer is the third most diagnosed tumor worldwide, it ranks second in terms of mortality, survival varies depending on the clinical stage at diagnosis.It is therefore a problem of great importance and magnitude with significant health expenditure.Objective: To describe the differences in the morbidity and mortality of patients diagnosed with colorectal cancer according to the place of study initiation (primary care vs. emergencies) and to evaluate the differences in the diagnosis of colorectal cancer in a geographic area after the implementation of the Prevecolon © screening program.Method: Descriptive, observational, longitudinal and retrospective study, 1,110 patients diagnosed and treated for colorectal cancer were evaluated at the Hospital Universitario Infanta Sofía, from March 8, 2008 to December 31, 2021.results: Of the 1,110 patients, 628 (56.6%) came from primary care and 482 (43.4%) from the emergency department.Fifty percent of the patients were diagnosed in advanced stages (III and IV).The diagnostic delay time was shorter in Emergency patients (p < 0.001), but mortality was almost twice in patients whose study began in Emergencies (p < 0.001).conclusion: Patients who begin the study for colorectal cancer in the emergency department present the disease in more advanced stages and show greater morbidity and mortality than those whose study begins in Primary care.

title: Predictors of 30-days favorable neurological outcomes following perioperative cardiac arrest with return of spontaneous circulation in non-cardiac surgery: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Background Cardiac arrest during anesthesia is rare, largely due to the presence of adequate equipment and personnel trained to promptly manage emergency situations. However, the causes, risk factors, and disease prognosis may differ from those of cardiac arrests occurring outside the operating room. This study aimed to identify factors influencing favorable neurological outcomes in patients undergoing surgery who experienced cardiac arrest and achieved ROSC during intraoperative period and within 24 h after surgery. Methods This retrospective cohort study was conducted at Songklanagarind Hospital, Thailand, and included patients between January 2010 and December 2022. A total of 314 patients who experienced perioperative cardiac arrest were identified. Of these, 166 patients aged ≥ 18 years who underwent non-cardiac surgery were included in the study, while 148 patients were excluded. An electronic medical record system was used to identify patients who underwent both elective and emergency surgeries. Patients were followed for 30 days after cardiac arrest. Neurological outcomes were assessed using the Cerebral Performance Category (CPC) score. Logistic regression analysis was performed to identify predictors of favorable neurological outcomes, and the predictive performance of the model was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Results Among the 166 participants who had ROSC included in the study. It was found that factors influencing 30-day favorable neurological outcomes included female sex (OR 2.98, 95% CI 1.09–8.16, p = 0.034), a fewer number of adrenaline doses (OR 0.85, 95% CI 0.74–0.97, p = 0.02), and lower sequential organ failure assessment (SOFA) scores at 24 h (OR 0.72, 95% CI 0.63–0.83, p < 0.001) with area AUC value of 0.879 (95% CI 0.803, 0.954) while shockable rhythm before cardiac arrest did not predict good neurological outcome (p = 0.588). Conclusion In patients with perioperative cardiac arrest who achieved ROSC, female sex, fewer adrenaline doses during resuscitation, and lower SOFA scores at 24 h were associated with favorable neurological outcomes at 30 days. These findings may assist clinicians in early prognostication and postoperative management following perioperative cardiac arrest.

title: Vessel-level patterns and predictors of discordance between computed tomography coronary angiography and invasive coronary angiography
abstract: BACKGROUND Coronary calcification is a recognized source of computed tomography coronary angiography (CTCA) stenosis overestimation. We evaluated whether discordance between CTCA and invasive coronary angiography (ICA) also shows clinically relevant vessel-territory patterns in a selected real-world paired-imaging cohort. AIM To evaluate patient- and vessel-level CTCA diagnostic performance, quantify territory-specific discordance, assess three-category stenosis agreement, and identify predictors of discordance in a selected paired-imaging cohort. METHODS We systematically screened the hospital CTCA database for October 2019-December 2024 and included consecutive adults with paired CTCA and ICA within 120 days, subject to the study exclusions. After reviewing interval revascularisation, we excluded one patient in whom percutaneous coronary intervention occurred after diagnostic ICA but before the subsequent CTCA, leaving 403 patients and 1612 major epicardial vessel observations. Severe/occlusive disease was the positive binary endpoint, with a left main coronary artery (LMCA)-specific severe threshold of ≥ 50% in both modalities. Patient-level predictors were assessed with logistic regression and vessel-level predictors with mixed-effects logistic regression using a patient random intercept. RESULTS ICA demonstrated severe/occlusive disease in 204/403 patients (50.6%). Patient-level sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) were 91.7% (95%CI: 87.0%-95.1%), 35.2% (95%CI: 28.6%-42.2%), 59.2% (95%CI: 53.5%-64.6%), and 80.5% (95%CI: 70.6%-88.2%), respectively. Across 1612 vessels, sensitivity was 80.8% (cluster-bootstrap 95%CI: 76.3%-85.1%), specificity 81.7% (95%CI: 79.5%-83.7%), PPV 50.4% (95%CI: 45.4%-55.2%), NPV 94.9% (95%CI: 93.5%-96.1%), and discordance 18.5% (95%CI: 16.6%-20.3%). At least one discordant vessel was present in 229 patients (56.8%). Discordance was highest in the left anterior descending artery (LAD) (31.8%) and lowest in the LMCA (2.5%). Three-category agreement was moderate (weighted kappa 0.500, 95%CI: 0.459-0.539). Calcium burden remained independently associated with discordance at the patient level [odds ratio (OR) = 1.66 per category, 95%CI: 1.03-2.73; P = 0.042] and vessel level (OR = 1.40, 95%CI: 1.04-1.87; P = 0.025). The LAD had higher adjusted odds of discordance than the right coronary artery (OR = 1.82, 95%CI: 1.32-2.53; Holm-adjusted P = 0.0003) and left circumflex artery (OR = 2.01, 95%CI: 1.44-2.80; Holm-adjusted P < 0.001). CONCLUSION In this selected cohort of patients who underwent both CTCA and ICA, greater visual coronary calcium burden was associated with anatomical discordance, and discordance varied by epicardial territory, being highest in the LAD. Because referral for ICA was selective, study readings were not independently blinded, and ICA stenosis was visually graded, the observed diagnostic metrics may not generalise to unselected CTCA populations. No downstream testing pathway, invasive-referral decision, or patient outcome was evaluated; the findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating.

title: PulseRoute: Smart Traffic Managemnt And Emergency Response System
INTELLIGENT CONSULTATION AND TRIAGE TECHNOLOGY BASED ON LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS AND MULTIMODAL VISION
abstract: In primary healthcare scenarios, patients’ chief complaints are highly colloquial and mix dialects with typos, and traditional rule-template-based triage systems struggle to map such expressions stably onto standard symptoms; the interpretation of laboratory reports and drug package images also relies on manual work, which limits efficiency. To address these two stages, this paper builds an intelligent consultation and triage system that integrates large language model semantic encoding, node-graph multi-turn consultation and visual multimodal recognition. At the system entry, a local keyword table performs fast matching first; when no hit occurs, the semantic mapping from colloquial description to standard symptom is handed over to the large language model. After entering the consultation flow, questions are asked level by level along a node-graph structure, and each round’s node is dynamically determined by the previous answer. The drug and laboratory report modules each follow a path of “local library first, model as fallback”, and visual recognition adopts Qwen-VL to complete drug name extraction and report structuring. On manually constructed test cases of colloquial, vague, typo-containing and multi-intent input, the system correctly enters the corresponding consultation flow in all cases. Test results show that, while maintaining response speed, this scheme has usable fault tolerance for non-standard input, providing an engineering-feasible implementation path for primary pre-diagnosis triage and medication education.

title: ICG fluorescence-guided lymph-node retrieval followed by postoperative immunohistochemistry in lower-extremity melanoma: an exploratory case series
abstract: Objective To describe our institutional experience with indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence-guided sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) followed by postoperative immunohistochemistry (IHC) in patients with lower-extremity melanoma, focusing on the observed intraoperative visualization and retrieval outcomes, pathological findings, technical difficulties, and procedural limitations of this sequential workflow. Methods This was a retrospective, single-center, descriptive case series. Fifteen patients with histologically confirmed lower-extremity melanoma underwent ICG-guided SLNB, of whom 13 had at least one pathologically confirmed lymph node retrieved. All harvested fluorescent specimens were examined by hematoxylin–eosin (H&E) staining and IHC for HMB-45 and SOX10 to detect micrometastases. Results Transcutaneous fluorescence visualization of lymphatic drainage was achieved in 13 of 15 patients (86.67%). A total of 21 fluorescent specimens were harvested, of which 17 were pathologically confirmed lymph nodes and 4 were non-nodal adipose/soft-tissue specimens. In two patients, fluorescent tissue was retrieved, but histopathological examination showed adipose tissue without lymph-node architecture. These patients were classified as pNx (pT2b and pT1b, respectively); preoperative imaging supported cN0/cM0 clinical status. H&E staining detected metastasis in 1 of 17 nodes (5.88%), whereas IHC identified micrometastases in 3 of 17 nodes (17.65%). No severe ICG-related adverse events or surgical complications occurred. Conclusion In this exploratory retrospective case series, ICG-guided lymphatic mapping was attempted in 15 patients and resulted in the retrieval of pathologically confirmed lymph nodes in 13 patients. IHC identified additional metastatic deposits within some of the retrieved nodes. Because no radiotracer comparator was used and no lymph node was retrieved in two patients, this study cannot establish the accuracy, completeness, or false-negative rate of ICG-only sentinel-node mapping. Larger comparative studies with standardized follow-up are required.

title: Construction of a nomogram for predicting pathological complete response of axillary lymph nodes in breast cancer after neoadjuvant chemotherapy using multiparametric MRI and clinicopathological features
abstract: Objective To create and verify a nomogram that combines clinicopathological variables and multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features to predict axillary lymph node pathological complete response (pCR) in patients with breast cancer after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT). Methods 287 breast cancer patients who underwent NACT and surgery at Yulin Xingyuan Hospital between January 2021 and December 2025 were included in this single-center retrospective cohort analysis. Of them, axillary pCR was attained in 111 cases (38.7%). Patients were split into a training set (n=201) and a validation set (n=86) at random in a 7:3 ratio. Electronic medical records, imaging systems, and pathological databases were used to gather clinicopathological traits, multiparametric MRI features, inflammatory markers, and immunohistochemistry indicators. Multivariable logistic regression was employed to find independent predictors after variable selection using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression. The receiver operating characteristic curve, calibration curve, and decision curve analysis (DCA) were used to evaluate the model’s performance. Results Six independent predictors were identified. Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (AUC: 0.660, 95% CI: 0.583-0.736), cortical thickening (AUC: 0.692, 95% CI: 0.630-0.755), and apparent diffusion coefficient mean (AUC: 0.739, 95% CI: 0.668-0.810) were the strongest predictors. The area under the curves for fatty hilum, Ki-67, and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 status were 0.628, 0.625, and 0.629, respectively. With Brier scores of 0.138 and 0.121, respectively, the nomogram’s area under the curve was 0.884 (95% CI: 0.838-0.929) in the training set and 0.888 (95% CI: 0.809-0.967) in the validation set. Clinical utility was established by DCA, and calibration curves demonstrated satisfactory agreement. Conclusion The nomogram combining NLR, clinicopathological factors, and multiparametric MRI features shows promising potential for predicting axillary pCR after NACT in breast cancer, though external validation is still warranted before clinical implementation.

title: Postoperative analgesia using the ERAS® protocol in total mastectomy. A randomized clinical trial
abstract: Background: Up to 60% of patients undergoing mastectomy for breast cancer experience severe postoperative pain.The Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS®) protocol has demonstrated efficacy in managing postoperative pain.Objective: To compare postoperative pain in patients undergoing mastectomy for breast cancer with and without the application of the ERAS® protocol.Method: Women over 18 years of age with breast cancer undergoing mastectomy were included.The ERAS® protocol was implemented during the preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative phases.Pain intensity was assessed at 0, 30, 60, and 120 minutes postoperatively, as well as at discharge.Results: A total of 80 patients were enrolled: 43 (53.75%) in the ERAS® group and 37 (46.25%) in the control group.A significant reduction in pain scores was observed in the ERAS® group during immediate postoperative assessment, at 30, 60, 90 minutes, and at discharge (p < 0.001).No significant differences were found between groups regarding operative time or intraoperative bleeding.conclusions: Implementation of the ERAS® protocol in patients undergoing mastectomy is associated with improved postoperative pain control.

title: Role of novel inflammatory indices in predicting major adverse cardiovascular events following revascularization in chronic limb-threatening ischemia
abstract: BACKGROUND Peripheral artery disease is a prevalent atherosclerotic condition leading to chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), which significantly increases the risks of limb loss and cardiovascular events. Despite advancements in revascularization techniques, long-term outcomes remain poor. AIM To evaluate the association of pre-procedural inflammatory indices with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) following lower-limb revascularization in patients with CLTI, and to assess the predictive performance of clinical models incorporating Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII), Systemic Inflammatory Response Index (SIRI), and Systemic Immune-Inflammation Response Index (SIIRI). METHODS A multicenter prospective observational study was conducted at two tertiary hospitals in Jordan, including 303 adults (≥ 18 years) with CLTI undergoing lower-limb revascularization between June and September 2024. Participants were followed for six months. Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics and pre-procedural inflammatory indices were obtained, and MACE was identified through follow-up and confirmed using medical records. Three multivariable logistic regression models were developed using the same clinical and laboratory covariates, with SII, SIRI, and SIIRI entered separately. The predictive performance of the SIRI-based model was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis and 1000 bootstrap resamples for internal validation. RESULTS The mean age of participants was 63.6 ± 9.8 years, and 84.5% were male. Overall, MACE occurred in 22.4% of patients. The incidence of MACE increased across Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection clinical stages, from 12.5% in the low-risk group to 17.7% in the moderate-risk group and 29.0% in the high-risk group (P = 0.038). Surgical revascularization was also more frequent among patients who developed MACE (30.5% vs 18.8%, P = 0.023). In multivariable analysis, SIRI was independently associated with MACE (odds ratio = 1.62, 95%CI: 1.156-2.279; P = 0.005). The SIRI-based model demonstrated strong discrimination, with an apparent area under the curve (AUC) of 0.937 (95%CI: 0.907-0.967), which remained robust after bootstrap internal validation, with an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.920. CONCLUSION SIRI was independently associated with MACE in patients with CLTI undergoing lower-limb revascularization and demonstrated strong discriminatory performance when incorporated into a multivariable clinical model. These findings suggest that SIRI may provide additional prognostic information beyond established clinical and laboratory characteristics and may have potential utility for cardiovascular risk stratification in this high-risk population. Further external validation is warranted before clinical implementation.

title: Subtherapeutic quetiapine concentrations and behavioral response in Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: Background Managing behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia in older adults with Alzheimer’s disease remains clinically challenging, particularly given the safety warnings associated with second-generation antipsychotics. Conventional therapeutic drug concentrations for quetiapine, derived largely from schizophrenia populations, may not apply to frail older patients, creating uncertainty regarding optimal dosing. Methods This prospective, single-center observational cohort study evaluated the effectiveness and tolerability of individualized low-dose quetiapine in older adults with Alzheimer’s disease and refractory behavioral symptoms. The full analysis set included 40 patients assessed using the Neuropsychiatric Inventory Questionnaire (NPI-Q), with an embedded pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) sub-study measuring steady-state trough plasma concentrations in 22 patients via therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) to explore the exposure-response relationship. The full analysis set (FAS) included 40 patients. Results Using a lenient but clinically relevant threshold, the overall responder rate (≥20% reduction in neuropsychiatric burden) was 97.5%, though no patient achieved complete clinical control. Notably, patients attaining marked improvement showed markedly lower median trough concentrations (19.3 ng/mL) compared to moderate improvers, with all measured levels remaining well below the traditional antipsychotic window of 100–500 ng/mL. Better-preserved baseline cognition and lower initial symptom burden predicted robust response. Quetiapine was well tolerated, with adverse events mostly limited to mild anticholinergic effects and asymptomatic corrected QT interval prolongation; no severe adverse events, extrapyramidal symptoms, or treatment-related deaths occurred. Conclusions Meaningful behavioral response was observed at plasma quetiapine exposures far beneath conventional therapeutic thresholds. While these real-world data suggest a potential role for cautious, blood-level-informed dosing strategies, they should be viewed strictly as hypothesis-generating pending validation in larger controlled trials.

title: Hydrogen Peroxide Irrigation-Induced Gas Embolism Leading to Cardiac Arrest During Surgery for Brucellosis Spondylitis: A Case Report
abstract: Hydrogen peroxide has both antibacterial and hemostatic effects, but it can cause fatal venous gas embolism (VAE), with a higher risk in patients with brucellar spondylitis accompanied by bone destruction. This article reports a case of such a patient who suddenly experienced cardiac arrest after intraoperative irrigation with 3% hydrogen peroxide, suggesting that clinical management during the perioperative period needs to be strengthened and the occurrence of VAE should be vigilantly guarded against.

title: Splenic Radiofrequency Ablation with Splenic Artery Balloon Occlusion for Hypersplenism in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
abstract: Background: Cytopenias can complicate antitumor treatment in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with portal hypertension-related hypersplenism. We examined treatment receipt, blood-count trajectories, and adverse events after splenic radiofrequency ablation (RFA) with splenic artery balloon occlusion. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort included 36 patients treated between August 2023 and November 2025. The primary descriptive outcome was antitumor treatment receipt within 60 days, including treatment on the procedure date. Additional outcomes included blood-count threshold attainment, adverse events, and exploratory oncologic outcomes. Results: Antitumor treatment was received by 21/36 patients (58.3%) within 60 days, including 8 treated on the procedure date, and by 28/36 (77.8%) during follow-up. Median platelet counts were 54.0 × 10⁹/L at baseline and 176.0 × 10⁹/L on day 7. Later laboratory observations were incomplete. Grade 3 adverse events were recorded in 15/36 patients (41.7%); no grade 4–5 events or procedure-attributed deaths were reported. Conclusions: In this selected cohort, early platelet increases and antitumor treatment receipt were observed. Same-day treatment and the absence of a comparator prevent attributing treatment delivery to hematologic recovery. Comparative studies are needed to determine whether this approach facilitates treatment and to characterize thrombotic and other complications.

title: Dynamic changes in perfusion index and their association with intraoperative thermoregulation during elective cancer surgery: a prospective observational cohort study
abstract: Background Intraoperative hypothermia remains common despite active warming. Perfusion index (PI), a noninvasive measure of peripheral perfusion derived from pulse oximetry, has been proposed as a predictor of hypothermia because peripheral vascular tone influences heat redistribution during anesthesia. However, its predictive value and relationship with core temperature remain uncertain. This study evaluated baseline PI as a predictor of intraoperative hypothermia and examined the association between serial PI measurements and core temperature during elective cancer surgery. Methods This prospective observational cohort study included 145 adults undergoing elective cancer surgery under standardized perioperative temperature management. Baseline PI was recorded before anesthesia induction, and nasopharyngeal core temperature was monitored continuously during surgery. Hypothermia was defined as a core temperature below 36.0 °C at any intraoperative time point. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses assessed associations with hypothermia, while receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis evaluated the discriminatory ability of baseline PI. Repeated-measures correlation assessed the within-patient association between serial PI measurements and core temperature, supplemented by exploratory longitudinal sensitivity analyses. Results In the primary analysis, 103 patients (71.0%) were classified as hypothermic, including 12 patients who were already hypothermic before anesthesia induction. Among the 133 patients who were normothermic at baseline, 91 (68.4%) developed incident intraoperative hypothermia. Epidural analgesia (p = 0.008), baseline PI <4.0 (p = 0.025), and greater estimated blood loss (p = 0.010) were associated with hypothermia in univariable analyses. After adjustment for baseline PI and intraoperative blood loss, epidural analgesia remained significantly associated with hypothermia (adjusted OR 4.54, 95% CI 1.24–16.59; p = 0.022), whereas baseline PI and blood loss were not independently associated with the outcome. Baseline PI demonstrated poor discriminatory ability (AUC 0.565), with an exploratory ROC-derived cutoff of PI ≤4.3 yielding 76.7% sensitivity and 50.0% specificity. Between-patient correlations between PI and core temperature were not statistically significant. Repeated-measures analysis demonstrated a very weak positive within-patient correlation (r = 0.123, 95% CI 0.083–0.163; p < 0.0001). Exploratory longitudinal sensitivity analyses indicated that this association remained small and was sensitive to the analytical approach. Conclusions Baseline PI demonstrated limited predictive value for intraoperative hypothermia in patients undergoing elective cancer surgery despite standardized temperature management. Although serial PI measurements showed a very weak association with core temperature, the findings do not support PI as a reliable standalone predictor of hypothermia or a surrogate for direct core temperature monitoring. Further studies incorporating detailed perioperative and time-varying hemodynamic data are needed to determine whether PI provides additional clinically meaningful information. Direct core temperature monitoring and appropriate warming measures remain essential.

title: Real-world safety profile of deflazacort: combined evidence from a single-center observational study, FAERS disproportionality analysis, and systematic review of adverse drug reaction case reports
abstract: Objective To comprehensively characterize the real-world safety profile of deflazacort, with a specific focus on the Chinese population, by integrating real-world clinical data, post-marketing surveillance signals, and published case evidence. Methods Data on single-center adverse drug reactions (ADRs) were collected through the National Rare Diseases Registry System from deflazacort-treated DMD patients at the Peking Union Medical College Hospital (PUMCH). Disproportionality analysis was conducted on the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) reports to identify safety signals, followed by a systematic review of related ADR case reports. Results Among the 63 enrolled patients in the PUMCH cohort, 71.4% (45/63) presented ADRs, with 137 ADRs documented. The most common ADRs were weight gain (26, 41.3%), Cushingoid appearance (16, 25.4%), growth retardation (15, 23.8%), and behavioral disturbances (13, 20.6%). The median onset time was 151 days (IQR, 54–341), with the highest proportion of ADR episodes observed around 1 year or later (23.9%). With the exception of one severe unlabeled ADR, Stevens–Johnson syndrome (SJS), nearly all reported reactions (136/137) were mild and label-consistent. Analysis of 3,351 primary suspected adverse events (AEs) from FAERS confirmed known signals and identified novel potential signals, including toe walking, fat embolism, and ligament sprain. Median onset was 231 days (IQR, 76.5–440), with the highest reporting rate (33.7%) typically emerging around 1 year or later. This case systematic review identified severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SCARs) as a critical adverse risk of deflazacort requiring close monitoring. Combining PUMCH and literature cases, 10 SCARs were identified, of which eight occurred in Asian individuals. Conclusion The results indicated a high overall incidence of deflazacort-related ADRs. Metabolic ADRs are typically observed around 1 year or later, whereas SCARs emerge within the initial 8 weeks of therapy. Asian patients were over-represented among the pooled SCAR cases; however, this observation cannot confirm the increased susceptibility and is limited by the small sample size and publication bias. Novel potential safety signals including toe-walking, fat embolism, and ligament sprain warrant further investigation, providing preliminary evidence for population-specific clinical monitoring and risk management.

title: Safety and feasibility of an ERAS-based tubeless day-surgery pathway for primary palmar hyperhidrosis: a single-center retrospective cohort study
abstract: Objective Primary palmar hyperhidrosis (PPH) significantly impacts patients’ quality of life. Although endoscopic thoracic sympathicotomy (ETS) is the standard treatment, minimizing perioperative trauma and enhancing recovery remain clinical priorities. This study aimed to evaluate the perioperative safety and short-term efficacy of a Tubeless day-surgery mode based on the enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) concept for PPH. Methods We conducted a single-center, retrospective observational cohort study including 82 PPH patients who underwent ETS between 2019 and 2026. Based on the anesthesia and perioperative management mode, the patients were divided into the conventional group (n = 51) and the Tubeless group (n = 31). Observation indicators included intraoperative safety indicators, postoperative recovery, complications, immediate postoperative efficacy, and compensatory hyperhidrosis 3 months postoperatively. We further employed propensity score matching (PSM) and overlap weighting (OW) models to adjust for baseline differences, and used the SMD to evaluate covariate balance. Results In the original cohort, there were differences in the distribution of surgical segments between the two groups. After PSM, a total of 28 pairs of matched patients were obtained, and after OW adjustment, the SMD of all baseline covariates was < 0.1, indicating good balance between the groups. Intraoperatively, the lowest SpO₂ in the Tubeless group within the original, PSM, and OW cohorts did not show a significant decrease, and the incidence of hypoxemia, surgery duration, and blood loss did not increase significantly. In the original cohort, the incidence of hypercapnia in the Tubeless group was higher; however, after PSM and OW adjustment, this trend did not reach statistical significance. Postoperatively, the Tubeless group exhibited lower incidences of cough and sore throat across all cohorts. There were no significant differences between the two groups in other complications, immediate efficacy, or compensatory hyperhidrosis. Conclusion The results indicate that the ERAS-based Tubeless day surgery model demonstrates certain feasibility for ETS. Compared with the traditional model, this model significantly reduced airway-related discomfort and did not increase surgery- or thoracic-related complications. However, due to the potential trend of an elevated risk of intraoperative CO₂ retention, continuous ETCO₂ monitoring must be performed. Further validation requires larger-scale, multicenter, prospective cohorts.

title: Bone Turnover Markers Improve Prediction of Adjacent Vertebral Refracture After Percutaneous Vertebroplasty: An Explainable Machine Learning Study
abstract: Objective To investigate whether bone turnover markers provide predictive information beyond conventional clinical risk factors for adjacent vertebral refracture after percutaneous vertebroplasty (PVP) in older patients with osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures (OVCFs), and to to develop an explainable risk stratification model. Methods We retrospectively included patients with OVCFs who underwent PVP between June 2019 and August 2024. The final analytic cohort comprised 1,730 patients, including 316 who developed adjacent vertebral refracture and 1,414 who did not. Patients were randomly divided at an approximately 8:2 ratio into a training cohort (n = 1,383) and an independent test cohort (n = 347). Eight prespecified predictors were evaluated: age, sex, body mass index (BMI), bone mineral density (BMD), β-C-terminal telopeptide of type I collagen (β-CTX), N-mid osteocalcin (N-OC), total procollagen type I N-terminal propeptide (tPINP), and 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25-OH-D). Six machine learning models were developed, including logistic regression (LR), decision tree (DT), random forest (RF), extra trees (ET), gradient boosting (GB), and extreme gradient boosting (XGB), and were evaluated in the independent test cohort. Model discrimination was compared using DeLong tests. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline analyses, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to characterize associations and model interpretability. Robustness was further assessed using feature-set restriction, 1st-to-99th percentile Winsorization, and threshold sensitivity analyses based on out-of-fold predictions from the training cohort. Results Among 1,730 patients, 316 (18.3%) developed adjacent vertebral refracture. In the independent test cohort, ET achieved the numerically highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.872 (95% CI, 0.829–0.915), whereas RF achieved an AUC of 0.869 (95% CI, 0.826–0.912); the difference was not statistically significant after Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment (P = 0.709). RF had the highest accuracy (0.818) and F1 score (0.583), with a Brier score of 0.106, and was therefore selected as the primary model for subsequent interpretation. SHAP analysis identified β-CTX as the most influential predictor, followed by BMD, N-OC, and 25-OH-D. In feature-set sensitivity analysis, the full RF model yielded an AUC of 0.862 (95% CI, 0.817–0.906), whereas a reduced model containing only the five bone-related variables yielded an AUC of 0.848 (95% CI, 0.801–0.896), with no significant difference between the two models (P = 0.339). In contrast, a model based only on age, sex, and BMI had substantially lower discrimination (AUC, 0.570; 95% CI, 0.494–0.646). After Winsorization, the AUC was 0.867 (95% CI, 0.824–0.910), which did not differ significantly from the original analysis (P = 0.078). Threshold sensitivity analysis further showed that lowering the classification threshold increased sensitivity and negative predictive value at the expense of specificity. Conclusions Bone turnover-related variables, particularly β-CTX, provide clinically relevant predictive information beyond conventional clinical characteristics for identifying patients at increased risk of adjacent vertebral refracture after PVP. An RF model based on eight routinely available variables demonstrated good discrimination and robust performance for internal risk stratification. However, given the retrospective design and imperfect calibration (calibration slope, 1.640), the model is currently better suited for risk stratification than for precise estimation of individual absolute risk.

title: Comparative Diagnostic Value of Astograph and APS Methods for Chest Tightness Variant Asthma in Children: a prospective randomized crossover study
abstract: Background The Astograph technique, based on forced oscillation technique, allows real-time monitoring of airway resistance during tidal breathing with better patient cooperation than conventional methods. However, its diagnostic utility for chest tightness variant asthma (CTVA) in children remains unclear. This study compared the performance and safety of Astograph and APS methods in diagnosing pediatric CTVA. Methods Children aged 6–17 years with chest tightness were enrolled from October 2023 to December 2024. Participants underwent both Astograph- and APS-based bronchial challenge testing in a randomized crossover design with 24–48 hour intervals. Subjects with airway hyperresponsiveness received anti-asthmatic treatment, and responses were monitored. Participants were categorized into CTVA or control groups based on final diagnosis. Results Of 132 enrolled children, 125 met criteria (CTVA: 51; controls: 74). CTVA patients showed significantly lower FEV1/FVC ratios and small airway parameters (p < 0.05), lower Dmin values, and higher SGrs and SGrs/Grs values (p < 0.05). ROC analysis revealed higher AUC for Astograph (0.777) versus APS (0.709). Diagnostic accuracy was superior for Astograph (83.2% vs. 80.0%). Astograph demonstrated lower adverse reaction rates (46.4% vs. 65.6%, p < 0.05) and shorter testing time. Conclusions Astograph method demonstrates superior diagnostic accuracy, safety, and efficiency compared to APS for pediatric CTVA diagnosis. PD25 represents the most valuable diagnostic parameter and is recommended for clinical implementation.

title: Spontaneous diaphragmatic hernia in a child: A case report and review of the literature
abstract: Background Spontaneous diaphragmatic hernia in children is rare and may occur without a clear history of trauma. When it presents acutely, respiratory and circulatory compromise can develop rapidly, making anesthetic management particularly difficult. We report an emergency pediatric case and describe the perioperative anesthetic strategies used according to the patient’s clinical condition.

title: Perioperative recovery and resection quality after endoscopic versus surgical resection of gastric gastrointestinal stromal tumors ≥2 cm: a propensity score-weighted cohort study
abstract: Background Comparative evidence on endoscopic versus surgical resection of gastric gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs) is largely confined to restricted size bands, anatomical subgroups, or single techniques. We compared short-term recovery and resection quality, rather than long-term oncologic outcome, across gastric GISTs of at least 2 cm. Methods Consecutive endoscopy-center and surgical-department records from 2016 to 2020 were harmonized and de-identified. A post hoc chart abstraction without a prior written protocol recovered margin status, specimen integrity, graded complications, blood loss, depth of mural involvement, and extended surveillance (20% abstracted in duplicate; kappa 0.79 to 0.91). Rupture was reclassified by the universal (Oslo) criteria, and complications were graded against one severity threshold in both arms. Analyses used propensity-score overlap weighting, alternative estimands, size-stratified interaction tests, and comparator restriction to completed laparoscopic or local/wedge resection. Results Of 262 patients, 105 underwent endoscopic and 157 surgical resection. Postoperative stay (median 7 versus 10 days), fasting duration (4 versus 6 days), and blood loss (24 versus 82 mL) were lower after endoscopic resection (all P < 0.001). Adjusted mean differences were −3.81 days for stay and −2.26 days for fasting, attenuating to −2.94 and −1.71 days against completed laparoscopic resection. Grade II or higher complications occurred in 7.6% and 9.6% (adjusted odds ratio 1.21, 95% CI 0.35 to 4.17). The universal criteria raised endoscopic rupture from 3.8% to 14.3%, reclassifying 13 endoscopic patients as high risk. One-piece endoscopic resection was achieved in 73.3% of tumors below 5 cm and 20.0% of those at 5 cm or larger, in which grade II or higher complications were more frequent after endoscopic treatment (33.3% versus 9.5%; P = 0.031; crude ratio of odds ratios across strata 14.6, 95% CI 2.2 to 98.7). Conclusions Endoscopic resection was followed by faster recovery in selected patients, although part of this advantage reflects differing departmental feeding and discharge conventions. Surgery delivered more reliable specimen integrity, and the technical and safety burden of endoscopy rose with tumor size. These findings support size- and anatomy-sensitive treatment selection rather than routine substitution of endoscopy for surgery; long-term oncologic equivalence could not be evaluated.

title: Mitochondria–endoplasmic reticulum contact remodeling and metabolic changes associated with 12-month major amputation after thrombectomy for acute limb ischemia
abstract: Background Mitochondria-associated endoplasmic reticulum membranes coordinate calcium signaling and cellular metabolism. Their relationship with major amputation after thrombectomy for acute limb ischemia remains unclear in humans. Methods This prospective, single-center cohort included 100 patients undergoing thrombectomy. Paired muscle biopsies were obtained immediately before and 30–60 min after reperfusion, with serial blood sampling and 12-month follow-up. The primary endpoint was major amputation of the index limb within 12 months. Mortality, reintervention, healing, and VascuQol-6 were secondary endpoints. Associations were explored using Firth penalized logistic regression. Results Within 12 months, 27 patients underwent major amputation and 73 did not, including four who died without major amputation. The mean perioperative increase in membrane contact length was greater in the major-amputation group (18.8 vs. 9.8 percentage points, nominal p < 0.001), accompanied by larger increases in MFN2, GRP78/BiP, HIF-1α, and tissue lactate. Diabetes, Rutherford class IIb, symptom-to-reperfusion time >12 h, contact-length increase ≥10 percentage points, and 24-h cell-free mitochondrial DNA ≥1,500 copies/μL were associated with major amputation in an exploratory five-predictor model. The apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.847 (95% CI 0.762–0.912), decreasing to 0.823 after bootstrap correction. Conclusion Perioperative changes in mitochondria–endoplasmic reticulum contacts and metabolic markers were associated with 12-month major amputation. The combined clinical and biomarker model showed promising discrimination within this cohort and may inform further study of postoperative risk assessment.

title: Clinical and polysomnographic characteristics of comorbid restless legs syndrome and obstructive sleep apnea: a hypopnea-predominant respiratory-event pattern
abstract: Introduction Restless legs syndrome (RLS) frequently coexists with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), yet the clinical phenotype of this comorbidity (Co-ROSA) remains poorly defined. We characterized Co-ROSA across presenting symptoms, sleep architecture, and respiratory-event composition—relative to RLS-only and OSA-only patients, and tested whether the body mass index (BMI) and apnea–hypopnea index (AHI) relationship differs from typical OSA. Methods We analyzed 1,213 adults with RLS (888 Co-ROSA, 325 RLS-only) and 2,963 OSA-only patients, using propensity-score matching (PSM), same-center sensitivity analyses, and a stricter AHI ≥ 15 threshold to assess the robustness of the findings. Results Co-ROSA presented as a clinical hybrid, reporting both breathing-related complaints (snoring 33%, witnessed apnea 7%) and RLS/sleep-onset complaints (leg discomfort 93%, difficulty falling asleep 49%), a profile intermediate between the two reference groups that persisted after matching to moderate-to-severe OSA. On polysomnography (PSG), Co-ROSA combined RLS-type sleep fragmentation and increased periodic limb movements with a hypopnea-predominant respiratory-event composition. Co-ROSA had a higher hypopnea index (HI), lower apnea index and apnea fraction than OSA-only (all p < 0.001); these differences persisted in an additional analysis matching the groups on AHI. In addition, AHI increased with BMI in both groups, but the BMI–AHI relationship showed attenuation at higher BMI levels in Co-ROSA compared with OSA-only. Discussion Co-ROSA was characterized by a clinical and polysomnographic profile combining hypopnea-predominant respiratory-event composition with an attenuated BMI-AHI association at higher BMI. This suggests that AHI-based thresholds may not fully capture disease characteristics in this phenotype and calls for phenotype-aware management.

title: 5G Network Slicing–enabled robot-assisted telementoring for simulated partial nephrectomy aboard a Role-2 naval platform: a proof-of-concept study
abstract: To evaluate the technical feasibility and operational workflow of a real-time robotic surgery telementoring system utilizing 5G Network Slicing technology between a land-based university hospital and a Role-2 amphibious warship stationed at sea. An experimental study was conducted between Kocaeli University Hospital and TCG Anadolu warship (equipped with a full Role-2 surgical capability) berthed in Marmaris. A mobile robotic surgery operating room integrated into existing ship facilities was established, and a remote expert-guided surgical operation was performed over a ~ 500 km network path using 5G infrastructure. The operating room was housed within a modular structure with a passive vibration-dampening system. Surgical simulations were performed across three independent sessions (2 ex vivo perfused porcine kidneys and 1 synthetic silicone organ model) using the da Vinci 5 (dV5) robotic platform. The surgical procedure was executed in two main stages: First, the remote expert dynamic-telestrated the parenchyma resection boundary on screen, and the bedside console surgeon completed the resection following these marked margins. Second, following the remote expert’s vector marking and technical guidance, a two-layer renorrhaphy (deep parenchymal and cortical closure) was performed using V-Loc barbed sutures. Medical data traffic was isolated using 5G Network Slicing; average end-to-end network latency was 21.4 ± 3.2 ms (range: 16–28 ms), jitter was 2.1 ms, packet loss was < 0.001%, and uplink/downlink bandwidths were recorded at 85 Mbps and 320 Mbps, respectively. In the simulated organ model, 7.8 min for determining the incision line and preparing, parenchymal resection time was 4.5 min and renorrhaphy time was 6.2 min (total surgical time: 10.7 min and total procedure duration 18.5 ± 2.1 min). The excised tissue segment measured 22 × 15 mm with zero positive simulated surgical margin. No clinically apparent/observable vibration-related disruption or visual degradation occurred during the procedure. These findings demonstrate that 5G Network Slicing-enabled robotic telementoring is technically feasible for delivering subspecialty surgical expertise to isolated maritime environments. However, this proof-of-concept is limited to dockside single-simulation sessions; clinical safety during open-sea transit, navigation, and varying satellite/terrestrial network conditions must be validated in future studies.

title: Electroacupuncture for post-stroke cognitive impairment: study protocol for a multicenter randomized sham-controlled trial
abstract: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) is a frequent complication of stroke that contributes to long-term disability, loss of independence, and reduced quality of life, while effective treatment options remain limited. This multicenter, parallel-group, randomized, sham-controlled, participant- and assessor-blinded superiority trial will evaluate the added efficacy of electrical stimulation and the safety of the study interventions when both groups receive protocol-specified acupuncture needling, standard medical management, and rehabilitation therapy. A total of 340 participants will be recruited at five tertiary hospitals in Hangzhou, China, and randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to an active-output electroacupuncture group or an inactive-output control group. Both groups will receive 40 acupuncture sessions over 8 weeks; electrical stimulation at 100 Hz will be delivered only in the active group. The co-primary outcomes are changes from baseline to Week 24 in the Mini-Mental State Examination, Montreal Cognitive Assessment, and Neuropsychological Test Battery scores. Secondary outcomes include neurological function, activities of daily living, sleep quality, depressive symptoms, health-related quality of life, electroencephalography (EEG), functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Safety outcomes comprise adverse events and serious adverse events. Clinical outcomes are assessed at baseline and Weeks 12 and 24, while neurophysiological and neuroimaging assessments are performed at baseline and Week 8. The trial will estimate the added efficacy of electrical stimulation and the safety of the study interventions in post-stroke cognitive rehabilitation. Clinical trial registration https://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn/, identifier ITMCTR2025000986; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07208019, identifier NCT07208019.

title: Squatting as a device-free remote ischemic conditioning stimulus: a hypothesis on habitual squat posture and reduced adverse events in atherosclerotic arterial disease
abstract: Atherosclerotic arterial disease remains the leading cause of death worldwide, and endothelial dysfunction is a pivotal, still-untargeted pathogenic mechanism across its natural history. Remote ischemic conditioning (RIC)—brief, repeated cycles of limb ischemia and reperfusion—protects the endothelium and remote organs in experimental and early clinical studies, but its translation failed in large perioperative randomized trials, plausibly because a single, passive, short-window stimulus cannot be expected to modify a chronic disease process. We propose a fundamentally different delivery strategy that requires no device: habitual squatting. Deep squatting and kneeling postures mechanically compress the popliteal artery and distal thigh vessels and may produce transient lower-limb ischemia. Whether the resulting tissue deoxygenation reflects true arterial occlusion rather than venous congestion must be demonstrated by direct flow measurement; this demonstration constitutes the first gate of the proposed research program. Emerging evidence shows that (i) squat-based exercise preconditioning protects endothelial function remotely, even in older and cardiovascular-risk populations; (ii) regular transient limb ischemia retards atherosclerosis progression in hypercholesterolemic rabbits in a dose-dependent manner; and (iii) daily ischemic preconditioning sustains endothelial protection in humans. We formalize the hypothesis that habitual squat-posture exposure acts as a chronic, self-administered, endogenous RIC stimulus, and we define an exposure-dose framework (frequency × ischemia duration × ischemia depth × cumulative years) suitable for epidemiological testing. The hypothesis generates testable predictions (including explicit falsification criteria) and a staged research agenda with pre-specified go/no-go gates. It also carries a unique quasi-experimental opportunity: the culturally embedded, facility-determined contrast between squat and sitting toilets in East Asia offers an exposure gradient that partially decouples squatting from fitness motivation. If confirmed, one of the most prevalent conditioning stimuli in human history could be repositioned from folklore to preventive cardiology.

title: CSF biomarker profiling reveals blood–cerebrospinal fluid barrier dysfunction in treatment-resistant schizophrenia in a naturalistic cohort
abstract: Treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS) affects ~25% of patients with schizophrenia, yet biomarkers for early identification are lacking. Here we retrospectively analyzed consecutively collected cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) from 260 inpatients who underwent lumbar puncture. TRS was defined by Treatment Response and Resistance in Psychosis (TRRIP) criteria (nonresponse to ≥2 antipsychotics at ≥600 mg chlorpromazine equivalents for ≥6 weeks). CSF measures included CSF/serum albumin and immunoglobulin (IgG/IgA/IgM) quotients, oligoclonal bands, pleocytosis and blood–CSF barrier (BCSFB) indices; we compared TRS (n = 32) and non-TRS (n = 151). TRS had longer illness duration, more hospitalizations, higher antipsychotic doses and lower functioning at discharge. TRS showed elevated CSF/serum albumin and immunoglobulin quotients, indicating BCSFB dysfunction without intrathecal immunoglobulin synthesis. BCSFB dysfunction was not explained by antipsychotic dosage or clozapine treatment. Machine learning identified BCSFB dysfunction as the leading biological TRS predictor. These findings implicate BCSFB dysfunction as a candidate biomarker of TRS that warrants validation in independent cohorts before potential clinical application.

title: Detection of eukaryotic micro-organisms in human clinical samples by shotgun metagenomics: read-based thresholds and determinants of performance
abstract: Bioinformatic detection thresholds for eukaryotic micro-organisms (fungi and parasites) remain largely undefined in human clinical shotgun metagenomics (SMg), limiting standardized implementation. We retrospectively compared SMg with standard of care (SoC) across 198 clinical samples from 187 patients to derive reads per million (RPM)-based detection thresholds for fungi and parasites across 5 major sample types. Total nucleic acids were sequenced (≥10 million reads per library) and processed with the MetaMIC ® v2.2.1 pipeline. Read counts were normalized as RPM. SoC identified micro-organisms in 152/198 samples (76.8%), spanning 44 eukaryote genera and 57 species; all 46 SoC-negative samples were also negative by SMg. The overall genus-level F1-score was 0.84, with performance varying by sample type: blood and biological fluids achieved the highest concordance (F1=0.98 and 0.97, respectively). Microbial load was the principal determinant of SMg sensitivity, with quantification cycle (Cq) values (n =57) inversely correlating with RPM (Spearman’s ρ =−0.66, P <0.001) and no false negatives at Cq<28.6. Receiver operating characteristic-derived optimal thresholds ranged from 0.06 RPM (faeces, Area Under the Curve [AUC] 0.91) to 0.57 RPM (tissue biopsies, AUC 0.90). A global threshold of 0.06 RPM yielded an AUC of 0.93 (95% confidence interval: 0.90–0.95; sensitivity 87.8%, specificity 90.7%). These results establish a quantitative, RPM-based framework for eukaryotic micro-organism detection in clinical metagenomics and a foundation for future multi-platform benchmarking studies.

title: Congenital heart disease in newborns - Advances in early detection, management and outcomes: A narrative review
