abstract: Congenital heart defects (CHDs) are among the most common congenital abnormalities and range from lesions that remain clinically silent in the neonatal period to critical defects that cause severe hypoxaemia, circulatory failure or death. Outcomes depend not only on lesion severity but also on timely recognition and access to specialist cardiac services. These challenges are particularly consequential in low- and middle-income countries, including Nigeria. To synthesise contemporary evidence on the spectrum, epidemiology, aetiology, clinical recognition, diagnosis, management, outcomes and prevention of cardiac anomalies in newborns, with emphasis on implications for Nigeria and sub-Saharan Africa. A targeted narrative literature update was undertaken for publications dated January 1, 2024 to August 31, 2026, supplemented by earlier landmark studies and Nigerian/African reports relevant to epidemiology and health-service context. PubMed-indexed literature and bibliographic records identified during the update were considered using combinations of terms for congenital heart disease, newborns, critical CHD, prenatal diagnosis, fetal echocardiography, pulse oximetry, management, outcomes, Nigeria and Africa. Relevant reviews, meta-analyses, epidemiological studies, clinical reports and guidance documents were synthesised thematically. This was not a systematic review; no pooled analysis or formal risk-of-bias scoring was undertaken. CHD prevalence estimates vary by population, diagnostic methods and setting. A 2025 African meta-analysis reported pooled estimates of 5.12 per 1000 in population-based studies and 12.63 per 1000 in hospital-based studies among children and adolescents, underscoring the effects of referral patterns and incomplete case ascertainment; these are not neonatal birth-prevalence estimates. Ventricular septal defect is commonly reported, and tetralogy of Fallot is a major cyanotic lesion. Prenatal assessment, newborn examination and pulse-oximetry screening can improve recognition, but no single screening approach detects every critical lesion. Echocardiography remains central to anatomical and haemodynamic diagnosis. Duct-dependent lesions require prompt stabilisation, consideration of prostaglandin E1 and urgent referral. Access to cardiac surgery, catheter intervention, intensive care and longitudinal follow-up remains unequal. Improving neonatal outcomes requires a coordinated pathway linking maternal care, prenatal detection, newborn screening, timely echocardiography, stabilisation, referral and definitive treatment. In Nigeria and comparable settings, screening programmes must be supported by diagnostic capacity, transport systems, specialist services and reliable surveillance.

title: Community-based management of nocturnal polyuria in older adults: protocol for a multicenter randomized controlled trial of a circadian-aligned dosing strategy using continuous digital monitoring
abstract: Background Nocturnal polyuria (NP) is a common age-related condition and a major contributor to nocturia, affecting sleep, quality of life, and healthy aging. Although desmopressin is an established pharmacological option, the risk of hyponatremia and the need for safety monitoring may limit its use in older adults. Guifu Dihuang Pill (GFDH) and Jinkui Shenqi Pill (JKSQ) are traditional Chinese medicine formulations used for urinary symptoms, but their efficacy and safety in NP and the optimal timing and duration of treatment remain unclear. This study aims to evaluate two dosing schedules for GFDH and JKSQ and explore response-guided treatment duration. Methods This multicenter, randomized, open-label, parallel-controlled trial will recruit 360 participants with NP from 11 community hospitals. Participants will receive GFDH (n = 240) or JKSQ (n = 120), with randomization within each formulation group to evening once-daily dosing or twice-daily dosing in a 1:1 ratio. Both regimens provide the same total daily dose of the assigned formulation. Treatment will last up to 8 weeks, with discontinuation permitted when predefined efficacy or complete remission criteria are met. The primary outcome is nocturnal urination frequency (NUF). Secondary outcomes include nocturnal urine volume (NUV), complete remission rates, and time to treatment response. Safety assessments include vital signs and adverse events. An intelligent urine-monitoring device will objectively record nocturnal urinary frequency and volume. Exploratory serum metabolomic analyses will be conducted in a randomly selected subset of 20 participants to investigate biological changes potentially associated with treatment response. Discussion By comparing circadian-aligned evening dosing with twice-daily administration of GFDH and JKSQ, this trial will investigate practical dosing strategies for community-based NP management. Objective digital monitoring and response-guided treatment duration may support more individualized care. The exploratory metabolomic analysis may generate hypotheses about biological pathways associated with treatment response. The findings may inform future clinical and mechanistic studies of NP management in older adults. Clinical Trial Registration Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR; http://www.chictr.org.cn; Registration No.: ChiCTR2300069136), registered on March 7, 2023; International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry (ITMCTR; http://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn/; Registration No.: ITMCTR2024000279), registered on August 21, 2024.

title: Perioperative inflammatory biomarkers predicting complications in implant-based breast reconstruction: a systematic review
abstract: Aim: To review preoperative and perioperative inflammatory biomarkers as predictors of surgical complications after breast reconstruction and assess whether reproducible cut-off values exist. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase (Elsevier) and the Cochrane Library were searched (January 2000-April 2026) following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. Two reviewers independently screened records using the population, intervention, comparator, and outcome (PICO) framework. Eligible studies quantified at least one systemic, fluid-based, or tissue-based inflammatory biomarker and reported its association with a defined surgical complication. Data were synthesized narratively due to heterogeneity. Results: Ten studies (771 patients, 377 reported reconstructions, 959 specimens; 2014-2026) met the inclusion criteria, all concerned implant-based reconstruction, and no autologous study was eligible. Biomarkers measured in systemic blood (n = 1), local fluid (n = 6), and capsular tissue (n = 3) addressed breast implant-related infection (BIRI), capsular contracture, and implant loss. Alpha-defensin-1 (AD-1) in pocket fluid was the only biomarker replicated across multiple cohorts, achieving sensitivity and specificity 100% and area under the curve (AUC) of 1.00 for BIRI, with a graded relationship to severity. Preoperative neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) independently predicted Baker grade III-IV capsular contracture, particularly after radiotherapy. Drainage-fluid intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1) and untargeted seroma metabolomics allowed pre-clinical detection. Tissue markers converged on myofibroblast-driven and estrogen-modulated mechanisms. All cut-offs remain externally unvalidated. Conclusion: Inflammatory biomarkers are promising but immature predictors of complications after breast reconstruction. AD-1 is the only biomarker with repeated evidence for BIRI; evidence for autologous reconstruction is absent. Future work should prioritize multi-center validation, harmonized outcome definitions, and biomarker-guided trials.

title: Analysis of risk factors for recurrence of phimosis in children after conservative treatment with topical steroids
abstract: Background Phimosis is a common disease in pediatric urology, and topical glucocorticoid therapy has been recognized as the first-line conservative treatment. However, post-treatment recurrence remains an important clinical problem, with reported success rates varying widely. Risk factors for recurrence after conservative treatment are not well defined. Objective To explore baseline, treatment-related and post-treatment factors associated with recurrence of phimosis in children successfully treated with topical corticosteroids, as an exploratory and hypothesis-generating analysis. Methods This was a single-center, retrospective cohort study that included 132 male patients aged 2 to 14 years who achieved a successful outcome (Kikiros and Woodward grade 0 or 1) following treatment with topical corticosteroids(0.1% mometasone or 0.05% betamethasone) between January 2023 and January 2025. Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics, treatment variables, and post-treatment adherence were extracted from electronic medical records. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with recurrence. Kaplan–Meier analysis was used to estimate recurrence-free survival. Results The mean follow-up was (12.1 ± 3.5) months, and the overall recurrence rate was 29.5% (39/132), with 79.5% of recurrences occurring within 6 months after treatment. In the final multivariable model, younger age (adjusted OR 0.51 per year, 95% CI 0.27–0.95; P = 0.033), severe initial phimosis (grades 4–5; adjusted OR 2.49, 95% CI 1.34–4.64; P = 0.004), balanoposthitis (adjusted OR 2.03, 95% CI 1.09–3.77; P = 0.025) and inadequate maintenance of retraction after treatment (adjusted OR 2.41, 95% CI 1.30–4.47; P = 0.005) were associated with recurrence. Preputial adhesion was associated in the fitted model (adjusted OR 2.32, 95% CI 1.25–4.32) but the association was unstable, being attenuated when the six boys with isolated adhesions were excluded (adjusted OR 1.36, P = 0.499). The age association also attenuated in older subgroups (age >=4 years: OR 0.77, P = 0.129). Treatment duration and time to treatment success were closely collinear and were not retained. The 6-month and 12-month recurrence-free survival rates were 76.5% and 70.5%, respectively. Conclusions In this exploratory single-center analysis, younger age, severe initial phimosis, balanoposthitis and inadequate maintenance of foreskin retraction after treatment were associated with recurrence, whereas the association with preputial adhesions was unstable and the treatment-response variables were collinear and uninformative. Because of the limited number of events and the retrospective design, these associations are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation before being used to stratify follow-up or to justify earlier surgical referral.

title: Effectiveness of thoracic radiotherapy for extensive small-cell lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) remains dominated by early intrathoracic and distant relapse despite first-line chemo-immunotherapy. The role of consolidative thoracic radiotherapy (TRT) in the contemporary era is uncertain. Hence, this review was performed to determine the effectiveness of thoracic radiotherapy for ES-SCLC. Methods We conducted a PRISMA-2020-compliant meta-analysis. Databases (PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and CENTRAL) and registries were searched till 13 November 2025. Dual-reviewer screening, extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment (RoB 2/ROBINS-I) were performed. Random-effects models synthesized overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), local-recurrence-free survival (LRFS), and grade ≥3 adverse events. Results Thirty-two studies (>45,000 participants) met the eligibility criteria. TRT improved OS [25 studies; pooled hazard ratio (HR) = 0.665, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.591–0.749]; this survival benefit was primarily driven by observational studies, whereas the limited pooled randomized evidence showed no statistically significant reduction in mortality. TRT also improved PFS (20 studies; HR = 0.626, 95% CI: 0.565–0.693). Pooled analysis suggested prominent local control benefit (LRFS, 5 studies; HR = 0.406, 95% CI: 0.301–0.547), though interpretation is restricted by the small number of reports. Grade ≥3 adverse events increased with TRT (18 studies; OR = 1.75, 95% CI: 1.41–2.17); single-arm pooled incidences of radiation pneumonitis and esophagitis were 11% (95% CI: 5%–18%) and 5% (95% CI: 2%–9%), respectively. Conclusion In ES-SCLC, TRT was associated with improved survival and thoracic disease control based predominantly on observational associations, but estimated OS benefit was substantially greater in retrospective than randomized evidence. TRT increased grade ≥3 adverse events. These findings support considering TRT for selected patients while underscoring the need for contemporary randomized trials. Systematic Review Registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261507557, identifier CRD420261507557.

title: Topical Wound Repair Formulation After Haemorrhoidectomy: A Randomized Controlled Trial
abstract: Delayed wound healing after haemorrhoidectomy may prolong wound exudation, postoperative pain and recovery. This randomized controlled trial evaluated the efficacy and safety of an investigational topical wound repair ointment compared with recombinant bovine basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF) and iodophor-based wound care. In this single-centre, randomized, assessor-blinded, parallel-group trial, 161 adults undergoing Milligan-Morgan haemorrhoidectomy were assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive the investigational ointment, topical bFGF or iodophor-based wound care. The primary outcomes were time to complete epithelialization and time to cessation of postoperative wound exudation. Secondary outcomes included granulation tissue formation, estimated wound area, postoperative pain and adverse events. Wound outcomes were assessed by blinded colorectal surgeons. A total of 161 participants were randomized (investigational ointment group, n = 53; bFGF group, n = 54; iodophor group, n = 54), and 150 completed primary-endpoint assessment. Median time to complete epithelialization was 29.0 days in the investigational ointment group, compared with 46.0 days in the bFGF group and 61.0 days in the iodophor group (log-rank p < 0.001). Time to cessation of wound exudation was also shorter in the investigational ointment group (24.5 vs. 42.0 vs. 58.0 days, respectively; p < 0.001). Granulation scores, estimated wound area and postoperative pain showed significant differences in longitudinal treatment trajectories (all time × group interaction p < 0.001). No serious treatment-related adverse events occurred. The investigational topical wound repair ointment was associated with faster complete epithelialization and earlier resolution of postoperative wound exudation than bFGF or iodophor-based wound care after haemorrhoidectomy, with a favourable safety profile. Larger multicentre studies with longer follow-up are warranted. Trial Registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR), registration number: ChiCTR2500097850.

title: Muscle attachment point acupuncture combined with physical therapy vs. physical therapy for chronic non-specific neck pain: a randomized controlled trial
abstract: Background Chronic non-specific neck pain (CNNP) is associated with persistent pain, functional disability, and restricted cervical range of motion (CROM). Whether symptom-guided acupuncture at muscle attachment points adds benefit to multimodal physical therapy remains uncertain. Methods In this single-center, assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial, 75 adults with CNNP were randomly allocated (25 per group) to acupuncture, physical therapy, or combined treatment for two weeks. Acupuncture at muscle origin and insertion sites was individualized according to the predominant symptom and administered in six sessions. Physical therapy comprised cervical manipulation, stretching, strengthening exercises, interferential electrotherapy, and red-light therapy (10 sessions). The combined group received both regimens. Pain intensity [visual analogue scale (VAS), primary outcome], neck-related disability (Neck Disability Index [NDI]), and CROM were assessed at baseline, week 1, and week 2. Results Sixty-one of the 75 randomized participants were included in the final analysis. At two weeks, VAS and NDI scores decreased significantly from baseline in all three groups (p < 0.01), without statistically significant between-group differences (p > 0.05). The group×time interaction was not statistically significant for all CROM directions (p > 0.05). Significant within-group improvements in cervical flexion, extension, and bilateral lateral flexion were observed in the combined treatment group (p < 0.05). However, no statistically significant between group differences were observed for any CROM measure at week 2. These within-group findings did not establish a statistically significant advantage of combined treatment over either individual intervention. No serious adverse events were reported; transient ecchymosis, dizziness, and neck discomfort occurred. Conclusion All three interventions were associated with short-term reductions in pain and disability. Although significant within-group improvements in cervical mobility were observed with combined treatment, its superiority over either individual intervention was not demonstrated. Larger trials with longer follow-up are warranted to determine the comparative effectiveness and long-term benefits of these interventions Clinical trial registration International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry (ITMCTR), ITMCTR2024000276; https://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn/mgt/project/view/-848051770134389942.

title: Clinical evidence for Astragali Radix-containing multicomponent formulas in chronic atrophic gastritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Chronic atrophic gastritis is a gastric precancerous condition characterized by gland loss and may coexist with intestinal metaplasia or dysplasia. Multicomponent botanical-drug formulas containing Astragali Radix are widely used, but their comparative effects require rigorous evaluation. Objective To evaluate the clinical efficacy signals and short-term tolerability reporting of eligible Astragali Radix-containing formulas for chronic atrophic gastritis. Methods Seven English and Chinese databases were searched from inception to 1 August 2026. Randomized trials were assessed with outcome-specific RoB 2 and GRADE. Meta-analyses used restricted maximum likelihood random-effects models with modified Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals and prediction intervals. Results Thirty-nine eligible reports were included; one was retained descriptively because arm-level outcome data were unrecoverable. For trial-reported overall clinical response, defined according to each study’s stated criteria, 33 studies were listed and 32 were estimable. The formulas were associated with a higher response rate (RR 1.25, 95% CI 1.19–1.30; I2 = 31.3%; prediction interval 1.12–1.39), and the direction remained stable across sensitivity analyses. Short-term endoscopic mucosal improvement consistently favoured the formula group (five studies; RR 1.32, 95% CI 1.13–1.55; prediction interval 1.10–1.59). Intestinal-metaplasia improvement also favoured the formulas (five studies; RR 1.42, 95% CI 1.10–1.85; prediction interval 1.06–1.92). Gastric atrophy showed a favourable average effect (five studies; RR 1.53, 95% CI 1.06–2.21), although its prediction interval crossed no effect; dysplasia and syndrome-score summaries were inconclusive. Helicobacter pylori eradication, recurrence, and adverse events were reported narratively because their definitions, denominators, or ascertainment were insufficiently comparable. Conclusion Eligible Astragali Radix-containing multicomponent formulas were associated with higher short-term clinical response, endoscopic mucosal improvement, and improvement in intestinal metaplasia. The consistency of these signals supports further clinical evaluation and standardization of these formulas for chronic atrophic gastritis. The magnitude and durability of benefit remain uncertain because of formula heterogeneity, predominantly high risk of bias, and limited standardized outcome assessment. Systematic Review Registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261429124, Identifier CRD420261429124.

title: Management of Performance Indicators in Public Hospitals: Evidence and a Research Agenda
abstract: Performance indicators support monitoring, resource allocation, and accountability in public hospitals, yet research on their management remains fragmented. This study examines how the literature has approached performance indicator management in public hospitals. A bibliometric analysis of 89 open-access documents indexed in Web of Science and Scopus was conducted, complemented by a document analysis of the full texts of 84 articles to identify the indicators investigated and the dimensions directly measured. The results revealed an expanding but fragmented field in which efficiency occupied a central thematic position, while quality and care remained recurrent themes. The complementary analysis showed that efficiency and productivity was the most widely represented category across articles, while length of stay, mortality, and bed occupancy were the most recurrent indicator concepts. Based on these findings, the study proposes a research agenda focused on multidimensionality, comparability, managerial use, and digital integration. By linking the field’s thematic configuration to the indicators examined in the full texts, it offers a literature-based reference for examining the composition of performance indicator sets reported in research on public hospitals and informing context-sensitive future research.

title: Service Disruption, Recovery, and Financial-Operational Context in a Public Tertiary Hospital: A Longitudinal Study of AIIMS New Delhi, 2010-2025
abstract: Background Public tertiary hospitals must sustain high-volume referral, teaching, and clinical services while managing constrained resources and external shocks. Longitudinal evidence integrating audited financial context, capacity, and multiple-service outputs is limited. This study examined long-term institutional expansion, the 2020–2021 service interruption, and subsequent service recovery at AIIMS New Delhi. Methods A retrospective longitudinal case study was conducted using publicly available annual reports from AIIMS New Delhi financial years 2010–2011 through 2024–2025. An institution-year series covered outpatient attendance, admissions, procedures, beds, occupancy, length of stay, and consolidated financial indicators; and a Center-year panel provided corroborative evidence. Long- linear trend models, exploratory segmented pulse-and-slope models, and Center fixed-effects models were estimated with robust uncertainty assessments and sensitivity analyses for approximate, missing, and definition-shift observations. Results Admissions increased by an estimated 3.71% per year (95% CI 1.21% to 6.27%) and reported bed capacity by 3.48% per year (95% CI 2.80% to 4.17%). In 2020–2021, outpatient attendance, admissions, and procedures were estimated to be 61.0%, 44.5%, and 62.1% below their fitted pre-shock trajectories, respectively, while bed occupancy was estimated to be 28.0 percentage points below its fitted trajectory. These are model-estimated deviations, not causal effects. By 2024–2025, outpatient attendance was 9.7%, admissions 34.7%, procedures 27.6%, and beds 31.0% above the observed 2019–2020 baseline, although occupancy remained 2.8 percentage points lower. Centre fixed-effects models provided within-source corroboration for outpatient and procedure disruption, whereas the admission estimate was imprecise. From 2019–2020 to 2024–2025, nominal income and expenditure increased by 70.1% and 68.4%, respectively. Conclusions AIIMS New Delhi experienced substantial but service-specific restoration of reported activity after a severe 2020–2021 interruption. Recovery is interpreted against both the observed 2019–2020 baseline and the fitted pre-shock trajectory, which are not equivalent benchmarks. The findings do not establish complete institutional resilience, technical efficiency, backlog resolution, or causal effects of the pandemic period, expenditure, or bed expansion on service restoration.

title: Missed and delayed documentation of postoperative delirium in older surgical patients and clinical outcomes: A retrospective cohort study
abstract: Objectives To describe missed and delayed clinician documentation of research-confirmed postoperative delirium and compare hospital stay and discharge destinations descriptively across documentation groups. Methods We retrospectively reviewed records of 271 surgical patients aged 65 years or older at a Melbourne tertiary hospital. Delirium was assessed prospectively using DSM-5 criteria during the first five postoperative days. Clinician documentation was classified as on-time (within 8 hours of researcher identification), delayed (more than 8 hours), or missed (no documentation). Baseline comparisons were unadjusted; outcomes across documentation groups were summarised descriptively without regression modelling. Results Delirium was identified in 44/271 patients (16.2%). Documentation was on-time in 9/44 (20.5%), delayed in 28/44 (63.6%; observed delays 24–72 hours), and missed in 7/44 (15.9%). Six of seven missed cases (85.7%) were hypoactive. Median hospital stay was 8 days with on-time, 14.5 days with delayed, and 7 days with missed documentation. New long-term care placement occurred in 4/9 (44.4%), 10/28 (35.7%), and 4/7 (57.1%), respectively. Patients with delirium differed substantially from those without delirium in age, cognition, dementia and surgical urgency. Conclusion Delayed and missed documentation were common. Hypoactive delirium predominated among missed cases. Differences in outcomes were unadjusted and do not establish an independent or causal effect of documentation timing. Repeated assessment and clear documentation warrant clinical attention.

title: Jejunogastric intussusception; case report of a rare long-term complication
abstract: Background Jejunogastric intussusception (JGI) is a rare complication following gastrojejunostomy (GJ) with a reported incidence of < 0.1%. The clinical suspicion, early diagnosis, and prompt management, can prevent a potential mortality which can be > 50% for a delay in the management. Case presentation: A 60-years-old male presented with acute severe epigastric pain associated with hematemesis, and diagnosed to have irreducible jejunogastric intussusception on endoscopy and CT scan. He had history of GJ done 20 years back for benign gastric outlet obstruction. He was managed with intussusception bearing jejunal segment resection and anastomosis and discharged to home in stable condition. Conclusion JGI is a rare, potentially fatal complication following gastrojejunostomy, can be managed successfully, if managed timely. Clinical significance: The knowledge of such a life threatening complication is necessary, to suspect the diagnosis and manage timely to avert potential mortality.

title: Managing suicide care in a low-resource urban context: stakeholder perspectives on system barriers and opportunities for improvement in Lusaka, Zambia
abstract: Objectives Suicide is a leading public health issue, and particularly a serious threat in low- and middle-income countries including Zambia. This study mapped the public healthcare system for suicide management in the 6 main hospitals in Lusaka and explored stakeholder perspectives on barriers and opportunities for improvement. Methods We conducted 32 semi-structured interviews with key informants. Data was analysed using a framework informed directed qualitative content analysis, supplemented by healthcare process mapping to identify system functions, barriers, and potential strategies for improvement. Results Stakeholders described a system centred on emergency departments and hospital-based care, often deprioritizing mental health once physical stability is achieved. Key challenges include insufficient staffing, lack of standardised discharge and referral protocols, and inadequate infrastructure for suicide care. Three areas for improvement emerged: training non-specialists, strengthening infrastructure, and standardised clinical pathways. Conclusion Addressing structural and workforce gaps in suicide and mental healthcare pathways is critical. These findings provide practical guidance for improving suicide care management to policymakers and health planners in Zambia and similar settings.

title: Wave overtopping load transmission and landward revetment stability on a sloping sea dike with varying crest widths
abstract: Introduction Wave overtopping threatens sea-dike landward slopes. Their stability depends on both load transmission across the crest and revetment resistance. Methods A calibrated 1:30 Froude-scaled model of a sloping sea dike in Zhejiang, China, was tested in a two-dimensional flume. A servo-controlled piston-type wavemaker generated shore-normal irregular waves using a JONSWAP spectrum. The tests covered four crest widths (8 -20 m), four wave -water-level conditions (100 -500-year return periods, 13% exceedance wave height H 13 % = 5.28 -5.66 m, and spectral mean period T = 15.5 -16.8 s), and four landward revetments. Overtopping pressure, flow velocity, discharge, and revetment response were quantified. Results Increasing crest width from 8 to 20 m reduced mean landward-slope velocity by 25.4 -30.5%. Widening from 16 to 20 m yielded a further reduction of 1.6 -5.8%. Pressures also decreased with crest widening. The 16 m crest under the 200-year condition had higher mean overtopping discharge than the 8 m crest under the 100-year condition (0.068 vs. 0.042 m³/(m·s)), but lower mean landward-slope velocity (approximately 2.3 vs. 2.6 m/s). Dry-stone damage progressed from stone loosening and local depression to stone loss and exposure of the dike body. Crest widening delayed clear instability until more severe conditions, although pronounced erosion persisted for the 16 and 20 m crests under the 500-year condition. The concrete revetment and nut-shaped blocks showed no visible instability. The four-corner blocks showed only transient local uplift for the 8 m crest under the 500-year condition. Discussion Crest width regulates load transmission, while revetment characteristics govern the resulting stability response. Assessment should consider mean overtopping discharge together with local pressure, flow velocity, and revetment stability.

title: Perioperative Pain Management in Gynecologic Oncology Surgery
abstract: Postoperative pain is a normal reaction to surgical intervention; however, it has been shown to increase morbidity, thus compromising the quality of recovery, which entails a delay in hospital discharge, increased risk of wound infection, and respiratory or cardiovascular complications, with an increase in mortality.Pain syndromes observed in patients with gynecologic oncology pathology result from three primary etiologies: those directly occurring due to the tumor, those deriving from treatments focused on reducing the tumor and those syndromes that are entirely independent of cancer or its treatment.Postoperative pain optimal management requires understanding the pathophysiology of pain and knowing the methods to be able to assess it in each patient, as well as knowledge on the different options available to control it.The key points that have to be considered are: the type of patient, type of surgical procedure, skills of the surgeon and anesthesiologist, and support of the working team.Improving the treatment of postoperative pain requires a broader perspective, since most healthcare providers have been shown to focus only on the postoperative period; however, ideal management is that where interventions are carried out before, during, and after surgery.(creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/).

title: Transvaginal small bowel evisceration twenty-two years after laparoscopic hysterectomy: A case report
abstract: BACKGROUND Vaginal cuff dehiscence associated with bowel evisceration is an uncommon condition. Very late presentation after hysterectomy can delay recognition because the original surgery may be overlooked. CASE SUMMARY An 84-year-old woman developed sudden transvaginal protrusion of the small bowel, severe abdominal pain, and urinary retention after 3 days of diarrhea and urinary symptoms. She had undergone total laparoscopic hysterectomy 22 years earlier. Examination revealed bowel congestion at the vaginal opening. Emergency laparotomy confirmed evisceration through the vaginal cuff defect with friable edges. A 50-cm ileal segment was herniated through the cuff. The compromised bowel was resected. The short, viable distal ileal remnant required right hemicolectomy and ileo-ascending anastomosis. The cuff was closed transabdominally in two layers. Early postoperative rigors and vomiting were managed with nasogastric decompression and antibiotics. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 8. Further documented follow-up data were not available. CONCLUSION Remote hysterectomy does not exclude the possibility of cuff dehiscence. Visible transvaginal bowel requires urgent surgical assessment and individualized management.

title: Acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis induced by ceftriaxone with tolerance to meropenem: a case series
abstract: Background Acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis (AGEP) is a severe cutaneous adverse reaction that carries a mortality risk and often presents due to a drug exposure. Guidelines advise against use of carbapenems in the setting of penicillin or cephalosporin induced severe cutaneous adverse reaction [1]. In critically ill patients this creates a dilemma regarding appropriate treatment when a patient reacts to a lifesaving agent, typically an antibiotic. Case presentation We present two patients who have each received ceftriaxone at least once with resultant AGEP in the critical care setting; both subsequently tolerated meropenem. Case 1: a 37- year-old male with significant past medical history of obesity hypoventilation syndrome, and cellulitis. This patient had two documented episodes of AGEP in response to ceftriaxone. The first occurred during an admission for hypoxemic respiratory failure and pneumonia. The second episode occurred two years later, following a single day of ceftriaxone for a respiratory infection, after which he was switched to alternative antimicrobials. The latency period was eight days after the first exposure and was three days after the second exposure. In both instances, the AGEP reactions fully resolved with supportive care. Subsequently, the patient tolerated two separate five-day courses of meropenem during admissions for pneumosepsis and cellulitis. Patch testing and intradermal skin testing with delayed reading were completed and negative for hypersensitivity to ceftriaxone one year after discharge from hospital. Case 2: a 63 -year-old male with no past medical history transferred from a rural hospital to a tertiary hospital intensive care unit for multi-focal ischemic strokes, seizures and bilateral pulmonary emboli. He developed pneumonia while admitted to critical care, resulting in ceftriaxone and vancomycin use. The latency period prior to development of AGEP was eight days after exposure to ceftriaxone. The AGEP reaction resolved with supportive care and change from ceftriaxone to meropenem. Patch testing and intradermal skin testing with delayed reading were not completed due to the patient’s passing from medical comorbidities. Conclusions This case series highlights two cases of critically ill patients that required admission to an ICU, received ceftriaxone and developed AGEP while tolerating meropenem without any cutaneous reaction or eosinophilia and with subsequent resolution of the drug reaction. Given the ubiquity of beta-lactams in the treatment of severe life-threatening infections, the ability to provide meropenem in patients with AGEP from ceftriaxone may prove lifesaving.

title: Clinical Profile and Functional Outcome of Osteoporotic Hip Fractures in Elderly Patients: A Prospective Observational Study
abstract: Background: Osteoporotic hip fractures are a major cause of morbidity, mortality and functional dependency among elderly populations worldwide. With increasing life expectancy and rising prevalence of osteoporosis, hip fractures are becoming a significant public health burden particularly in developing countries. Functional recovery after hip fracture is often incomplete and many patients fail to regain pre-fracture independence. Objective: To evaluate the clinical profile and functional outcomes of elderly patients with osteoporotic hip fractures and identify factors influencing recovery. Methods: This prospective observational study was conducted among 60 elderly patients (≥60 years) admitted with osteoporotic hip fractures at the Department of Orthopedics, Universal Medical College Hospital, Dhaka, Bangladesh from July to December 2025. Demographic data, comorbidities, fracture patterns, surgical details and postoperative outcomes were recorded. Functional outcomes were assessed using the Harris Hip Score (HHS) and ability to perform activities of daily living (ADL) over a 6-month follow-up period. Results: The mean age of patients was 74.8 ± 8.6 years with female predominance (68.3%). Intertrochanteric fractures were the most common type (55%). Hypertension (58.3%) and diabetes mellitus (41.6%) were frequent comorbidities. Surgical management was performed in 85% of cases. At 6 months, only 38.3% of patients regained independent ambulation. Mean HHS improved from 32.4 ± 6.2 at discharge to 71.6 ± 10.8 at 6 months. Mortality rate during follow-up was 10%. Poor functional outcome was significantly associated with advanced age, delayed mobilization and multiple comorbidities. Conclusion: Osteoporotic hip fractures in elderly patients result in substantial functional impairment. Early surgery, multidisciplinary care and structured rehabilitation significantly improve functional outcomes.

title: Letter to the Editor: Risk-stratified observation windows in outpatient percutaneous coronary intervention
abstract: For outpatient or same-day discharge after an uncomplicated elective percutaneous coronary intervention, consensus statements and society guidance frequently utilize a pragmatic post-procedure observation window of 4 hours to 6 hours in uncomplicated patients. Although clinical trials and registries show that acute ischemic and vascular complications predominantly cluster within the initial 2 hours to 6 hours or after 24 hours, significant clinical heterogeneity and varying hemostasis protocols exist across real-world practice. In the work published in the World Journal of Cardiology , Klocek et al reported a substantial cohort of 444 patients who underwent a total of 787 percutaneous coronary intervention procedures and were discharged after a median observation window of 150 minutes (ranging from 65 minutes to 523 minutes), suggesting that ultra-short observation may be feasible in selected settings. In this correspondence, we emphasize three key priorities to optimize clinical applicability: (1) Establishing a standardized operational definition of the observation interval (e.g. , from sheath removal, hemostasis achievement, or recovery arrival); (2) Delineating institutional pre- and post-procedure discharge-selection criteria; and (3) Reporting granular, risk-stratified patient and procedural profiles across discrete monitoring windows alongside minor access-site complications and patient-reported outcomes.

title: Understanding the 2026 Bundibugyo Ebola Virus Disease Outbreak in Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo: Epidemiological Trends and Health-System Response Constraints
abstract: Background: The 2026 Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease (BDBV) outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), primarily affecting Ituri Province, represents the largest documented outbreak caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus since its identification in Uganda in 2007. The outbreak unfolded in a complex humanitarian and security environment characterized by armed conflict, population displacement, mining-related mobility, constrained health-system capacity, misinformation, and declining public trust. This study aimed to describe the epidemiological characteristics of the outbreak and assess the operational challenges affecting the implementation of response activities. Methods: An integrated assessment comprising two complementary components was conducted. First, a rapid operational field assessment was undertaken from 12–15 June 2026 in Bunia, Rwampara Health Zone, and the Ituri Provincial Public Health Laboratory. This component involved direct observations, health-facility and laboratory assessments, document reviews, and stakeholder consultations to examine surveillance, contact tracing, laboratory capacity, clinical care, infection prevention and control (IPC), logistics, risk communication, community engagement, and infodemic management. Second, a descriptive epidemiological analysis of routine outbreak surveillance situation reports was conducted using data available up to 10 July 2026. Epidemiological indicators were summarized descriptively, and the temporal distribution of reported cases and deaths was examined using an epidemic curve. Results: By 10 July 2026, the outbreak had resulted in 1,877 laboratory-confirmed cases and 675 deaths nationally, corresponding to a case fatality ratio of 36.0%. Ituri Province accounted for 90.8% of confirmed cases (1,705/1,877) and 85.5% of reported deaths (577/675). Surveillance reports documented 766 alerts, of which 678 (88.5%) were investigated, identifying 235 suspected cases. Of 6,475 registered contacts, 4,171 (64.4%) were successfully followed, below the recommended target of ≥95%. Among 137 specimens tested, 29 (21.2%) were positive. Treatment-centre reports documented 61 admissions, 14 deaths, and an occupancy rate of 97.3% during the reported period. The June field assessment identified substantial operational constraints, including limited treatment capacity, shortages of trained personnel and essential IPC supplies, laboratory and logistical challenges, insecurity, delayed case investigations, and inconsistencies in surveillance data. Community resistance, misinformation, rumors, attacks on burial teams, and declining public trust further complicated care-seeking, contact tracing, and safe burial practices. Conclusions: The 2026 BDBV outbreak illustrates the complex interaction between epidemiological, health-system, security, and sociocultural factors influencing outbreak response in conflict-affected settings. The integration of field observations and routine surveillance data provides complementary insights into the progression of the outbreak and the operational constraints affecting its control. Strengthening surveillance, contact tracing, laboratory capacity, clinical care, IPC, and response coordination, alongside context-sensitive risk communication and meaningful community engagement, is essential to improving outbreak control and preparedness in eastern DRC and the wider Great Lakes region.

title: Impact of primary tumor resection in patients with metastatic breast cancer
abstract: Objective: Evaluate the impact of modified radical mastectomy on overall survival and progression free period of patients with stage IV breast cancer treated at the ISSEMyM State Cancer Center.Material and Methods: An observational, retrospective, and historical cohort study where patients with metastatic breast cancer from the ISSEMyM State Cancer Center were reviewed.The efficacy of surgical treatment of the primary tumor with Kruskal-Wallis test was evaluated.Comparing overall survival and progression-free survival in both groups.OS and PFS were calculated at 5 years with Log-Rank test plotted on Kaplan and Meier curves.Cox multivariate analysis was used to calculate the adjusted risks expressed with Hazard ratio (HR) 95% confidence interval (CI).Results: We identified 96 patients with metastatic breast cancer.46 (48%) were excluded because they received surgical management prior to referral, unjustified suspension of established medical-surgical management and/or failure to continue with regular follow-up.Of the 50 (52%) patients included for the analysis, 34 (65%) underwent surgery and 16 (35%) did not.The mean age was 54 years (s = ± 13).No metastasectomy.All with radiotherapy to the surgical bed at doses of 32.6-60 Gy.The overall survival, reported in months and according to the univariate analysis, was higher for the operated ones than for those that did not (28.5 months [range 6-74.[3] vs. 9.7 months [range 0.8-39.[2],p = 0.001).Similarly PFS was higher for patients operated on [20].6 months (range 5.7-77.3)]than for the non-operated 7.5 months (range 0.7-17.0)](p <0.0001).However, in the multivariate analysis "marginal" and non-statistical significance of the surgery in the OS were identified (HR = 0.35, 95% CI 0.12-1.03[p = 0.057]); but a positive impact on PFS (HR = 0.2, 95% CI 0.07-0.56[p = 0.0021]).Surgery improved PFS in oligomethasic disease (HR = 0.361, 95% CI 0.14-0.93[p = 0.035]).And offered worse OS for the molecular subgroups: Triple negative (HR = 5.56, 95% CI 1.03-29.97[p = 0.045]) and Luminal B/ with Her2 + overexpression (HR = 8.9, 95% CI 1.28-61.83[p = 0.027]).Conclusions: Our findings suggest that resection of the primary tumor in patients with metastatic breast cancer treated in the ISSEMyM State Cancer Center has a favorable impact on its PFS and borderline overall survival, particularly benefiting patients with oligomethasic disease in whom although the surgery did not help them to live longer we could say that it impact in favor of a greater PFS.In addition, the findings obtained in this study suggest that such intervention should be avoided in patients with a Luminal B profile with Her2+ overexpression and triple negative because they lack benefit in both OS and PFS, since the aggressive biology of these neoplasms, does not seem to give enough time for the mastectomy to add any benefit to the OS and/or PFS.

title: Integrated Care Models and Hospital Readmission Rates
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Integrated care is widely proposed as a way of reducing hospital readmission, yet the term covers programs as different as a nurse's home visit after discharge and a pooled budget for a whole region. This paper combines a synthesis of secondary evidence with an analytical model and an econometric analysis of hospital data. The synthesis rests on systematic reviews, trials, observational evaluations, and official reports, 100 references in all, each confirmed against its bibliographic record or source page; it is not a formal systematic review. The sources are sorted into four types: episode-bound transitional care, continuing disease management, organizational and financial integration, and integrated delivery systems. Intensive, multi-component transitional programs reduce readmission modestly, with pooled relative risks of 0.82 and 0.89 in two syntheses and the clearest support in heart failure, where the most recent meta-analysis rates its certainty as very low. Care coordination for patients at high need and a multimodal program for patients at high risk gave null results in randomized trials. Readmission fell in the United States under the Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program, but part of the measured fall depends on how observation stays are classified, and a regression-kink analysis found little effect. English pooled-fund programs were evaluated against delayed transfers and emergency admissions, not readmission. A model of transitional-care effort under a readmission penalty shows that the avoidable share sets a floor on the attainable relative risk, about 0.73 if 26.9 percent of readmissions are preventable. In Medicare data for 3,989 hospitals, meeting federal criteria for electronic record interoperability was associated with a hospital-wide readmission rate 0.04 points lower (not significant), while a hospital-wide component accounted for an intraclass correlation of 0.32 across four condition-specific rates. Evidence on cost, equity, and low- and middle-income settings, including Nigeria, is thin. Keywords: integrated care; hospital readmission; transitional care; Better Care Fund; Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program; heart failure; evidence synthesis

title: Clinical and Economic Outcomes of Microsurgery Versus Standard Craniotomy for Intracranial Tumors: A 15-Year Nationwide Analysis in Brazil
abstract: Introduction Intracranial tumors require highly complex surgical interventions. Standard craniotomies have been progressively replaced by microsurgical techniques to improve outcomes. However, the large-scale impact of this technological transition within the Brazilian public health system (SUS) remains underexplored. Objective To compare the surgical volume, regional distribution, hospitalization metrics, and mortality between standard craniotomies and microsurgical resections for intracranial tumors in Brazil. Methods A retrospective analytical study was conducted using hospital production data (SIH/SUS) from DATASUS (2010–2025). Procedures were grouped into “Standard Craniotomy” (codes 0403030030/0403030048) and “Microsurgery” (0403030145/0403030153). Variables included total volume, regional distribution, average length of stay (ALOS), costs, and mortality. ALOS significance was determined via Welch’s t-test. Results A total of 98,163 procedures for intracranial tumor resection were performed. The Microsurgery cohort accounted for 75.7% (n = 74,344) of the surgeries, and the Standard Craniotomy cohort represented 24.3% (n = 23,819). Temporally, craniotomies faced a 63.4% reduction from 2010–2025, whereas microsurgeries increased by 51.1%. Geographically, a severe disparity was observed; the Southeast region concentrated the vast majority of high-complexity microsurgeries (44.0%, n = 32,712), whereas the North accounted for merely 7.5% (n = 5,576). Clinically, the Microsurgery group demonstrated a significantly shorter average hospitalization period (13.4 ± 1.4 days) compared to the Standard Craniotomy group (15.3 ± 1.0 days; P < 0.001), indicating faster patient recovery and improved hospital bed turnover. The overall mortality rate was notably lower in the microsurgical cohort (6.80%) versus the macroscopic approach (8.38%). Economically, average direct cost per hospitalization was higher for microsurgery (BRL 6,386 vs. BRL 5,136). However, the significant reduction of nearly 2 days in length of stay suggests a broader systemic cost-effectiveness that offsets the initial procedural expense. Conclusion The surgical management of intracranial tumors in Brazil shows a highly beneficial transition towards microsurgery. This technique yields superior clinical endpoints—shorter stays and lower mortality—despite higher direct costs. However, the marked geographic concentration underscores an urgent need for decentralized investments to ensure equitable neuro-oncological care.

title: Damage control surgery and stoma-free negative pressure wound therapy for Fournier's gangrene with retroperitoneal extension: a case report
abstract: Background Fournier's gangrene (FG) is a fulminant necrotizing fasciitis of the perineal, genital, and perianal regions, and reported mortality ranges from 10% to 40%. Outcomes deteriorate further when septic shock and retroperitoneal extension coexist. Guidelines recommend prompt, thorough debridement, but in this subgroup radical excision may breach the peritoneal cavity or cause massive haemorrhage, and the role of damage control surgery (DCS) is poorly defined. We describe a patient with FG extending to the retroperitoneum managed with staged DCS, a stoma-free negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) assembly, and early function-oriented rehabilitation. Case presentation: A 36-year-old male labourer with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus was transferred after 18 days of treatment elsewhere for septic shock, Klebsiella pneumoniae bacteraemia, and necrotizing fasciitis that had persisted despite three debridements. He had full-thickness necrosis of the lower abdominal wall, both groins, perineum, and scrotum, with retroperitoneal and pelvic extension and sinus tracts reaching the peritoneal plane, without bowel involvement or peritoneal perforation. Because radical excision was judged too hazardous, necrotic fascia was removed incrementally at repeated operations while tissue in the zone of stasis was preserved; a modified NPWT assembly (anal tube, perianal adhesive sealant, continuous irrigation) combined with mechanical bowel preparation and a residue-free diet avoided diverting colostomy. Culture-guided antimicrobials, glycaemic control, nutritional support, endoscopic clipping of two bleeding points on day 7, and rehabilitation from admission completed the programme. Nine operations were required; flap transfer and skin grafting achieved closure on day 37, and he was discharged on day 114. Lower-limb muscle strength recovered from Medical Research Council grade 1 to grade 4, and at four months he had returned to independent living and manual work without recurrence. Conclusions In selected patients with FG and retroperitoneal extension who have no bowel perforation, clostridial progression, or uncontrolled haemorrhage, staged DCS with stoma-free NPWT and early rehabilitation proved feasible and preserved function. A single case cannot establish efficacy; the report offers a management template and a hypothesis for prospective study.

title: Preoperative frailty and length of hospital stay after coronary artery bypass grafting
abstract: Preoperative frailty - characterized by reduced physiological reserve, muscle strength, and endurance - significantly increases both 30-day and long-term mortality following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery. Data show that frail individuals face up to a twofold to threefold higher risk of perioperative death and higher rates of complications such as acute kidney injury. However, data for the association between preoperative frailty assessed by physical activity and handgrip strength and length of hospital stay after CABG are inconsistent. In this editorial, we discuss a recently published study by Nazir et al in the World Journal of Cardiology and the discrepancy, which may reflect the predominant influence of acute surgical complications and non-clinical discharge determinants over baseline functional metrics.

title: Artificial intelligence for caesarean surgical site infection surveillance: A scoping review of risk prediction, detection and clinical translation
abstract: Background Caesarean surgical site infection (cSSI) can prolong recovery, increase costs and require readmission. Surveillance is challenging after discharge, when wound changes may go unnoticed and travel, cost and limited clinical access delay assessment. Artificial intelligence (AI) could support risk stratification and infection detection, but its clinical value depends on performance and integration into maternal care. This review mapped AI applications for cSSI and examined clinical translation using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR). Methods This scoping review followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews and was preregistered on the Open Science Framework (DOI: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/JCXD2). Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to 14 October 2026, supplemented by Google Scholar citation searching. Two independent reviewers screened records. English-language studies reporting cSSI and AI-assisted surveillance were eligible. Study characteristics, applications, performance, and validation were charted and synthesised descriptively. Implementation-relevant findings were mapped to the updated CFIR domains. Performance estimates were not pooled because of methodological and clinical heterogeneity. Results Eight studies published between 2019–2026 from Rwanda, the United States and Australia. Applications included clinical-data risk prediction, colour and thermal wound-image classification, smartphone-based image processing and language-model auditing of clinical notes. The largest caesarean-specific study included 5,272 deliveries. Its area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), declined from 0.78 during training to 0.69 [95% confidence interval 0.63–0.75] in external testing, indicating modest discrimination in a separate population. Colour-image models reported median AUC of 0.639–0.655, whereas thermal transfer learning achieved 0.90 using only 30 infected wounds and internal evaluation. A language-model audit achieved 93% patient-level accuracy with 100% sensitivity and 86% specificity in 28 mixed-surgery patients. CFIR mapping identified acquisition standardisation, adaptation and information infrastructure as translation considerations; leadership, sustained financing, recipient engagement and implementation outcomes were insufficiently examined. No study demonstrated improved maternal postoperative outcomes attributable to AI deployment. Conclusions AI offers potential support for cSSI surveillance, but technical performance does not establish clinical effectiveness. Clinical translation requires independent validation and prospective evaluation of human-supervised pathways, including timely assessment, equitable access, staff workload and sustainable intervention delivery.

title: Robot-assisted stereotactic catheter drainage vs. standard medical treatment for 20–30 mL basal ganglia intracerebral hemorrhage: a propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study
abstract: Objective: To investigate whether robot-assisted stereotactic catheter drainage was associated with better functional recovery than standard medical treatment in selected patients with basal ganglia intracerebral hemorrhage (BGICH) and a hematoma volume of 20–30 mL. Methods This single-center, retrospective, propensity score-matched cohort study included patients with BGICH treated at Shenyang First People's Hospital of Liaoning Province between June 2022 and December 2025. Patients were classified into the operation or non-operation group according to the treatment actually received in routine clinical practice. Propensity score matching was performed to reduce baseline imbalance and treatment-selection bias. Short-term neurological recovery, in-hospital outcomes, and 90-day functional outcomes were compared between the two groups in the matched cohort. Results Among 287 screened patients, 165 met the eligibility criteria, including 103 patients in the operation group and 62 in the non-operation group. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 53 matched pairs were included in the primary analysis, with adequate balance in baseline characteristics. Compared with the non-operation group, the operation group had a shorter length of hospital stay, higher upper- and lower-limb muscle strength at discharge, and higher rates of limb muscle strength improvement. At 90 days after symptom onset, the operation group had lower modified Rankin Scale scores and higher Glasgow Outcome Scale and Karnofsky Performance Scale scores than the non-operation group. No significant differences were observed in common in-hospital complications or in the recovery of dysphagia or dysarthria. Conclusion In selected patients with 20–30 mL BGICH, robot-assisted stereotactic catheter drainage was associated with better early limb motor recovery, shorter hospitalization, and more favorable 90-day functional outcomes. Because treatment was not randomized and post-discharge rehabilitation exposure was incompletely quantified, these findings are exploratory. Further assessment using prospective data is warranted.

title: Prognostic Factors in Patients Diagnosed with High Grade Glioma Managed with Radiotherapy: Experience at the Federico Gómez Children’s Hospital of Mexico
abstract: Introduction: High-grade gliomas account for 15-20% of intracranial tumors in the pediatric population, usually with poor prognosis for overall survival.Objective: To identify prognostic factors for overall survival and local control in patients diagnosed with intracranial high-grade gliomas managed with conformal radiotherapy.Patients and methodology: This retrospective study assessed all high-grade glioma-diagnosed patients treated with radiotherapy at the Federico Gómez Children's Hospital over the period 2008-2013 by means of a review of medical records, imaging files, and treatment plans.Results: The analyzed patients (n = 18) had a median age of five years.The most common localization was infratentorial.Histologies found were glioblastoma multiforme and anaplastic astrocytoma.Of the analyzed patients, 44.4% received surgical management owing to the lesion localization and their performance status.All patients received radiotherapy with > 54 Gy total dose with or without chemotherapy.Local control rate was 94.4% and median overall survival was 13 months.With regard to surgical management for gross tumor resection, subtotal tumor resection, and no resection, five-year overall survival was 100, 50, and 36%, respectively (p = 0.04).The patients showed overall survival improvement with radiotherapy total dose > 54 Gy and standard fractioning.Conclusion: In the present study, surgical gross resection and management with standard external beam radiotherapy at doses > 54 Gy were found to be predictive factors for overall survival in pediatric patients diagnosed with intracranial highgrade gliomas.(creativecommons.org/

title: Measuring what matters in geriatric trauma: The mobility independence levels for safe discharge score
journal: Journal of Musculoskeletal Surgery and Research
abstract: Traditional outcome measures in geriatric trauma, including mortality, complications, radiographic healing, and length of hospital stay, provide limited insight into functional recovery and discharge readiness. This narrative review introduces the mobility independence levels evaluation score for safe discharge (MILES), a conceptual framework designed to assess the mobility-related component of discharge readiness following geriatric trauma. The secondary aim is to examine the physiological and functional consequences of trauma in older adults from a mobility-centered perspective. A narrative review of the literature was conducted, synthesizing evidence on frailty, functional reserve, immobility-related complications, quality of life, caregiver burden, rehabilitation, and existing outcome measures. Current trauma, frailty, and mobility assessments were examined to identify gaps in evaluating functional recovery and discharge readiness. Recovery after geriatric trauma depends not only on injury severity but also on vulnerability to immobility and loss of functional independence. Existing trauma severity scores quantify injury burden, while frailty measures estimate biological vulnerability; however, neither directly assesses the progressive mobility abilities relevant to discharge readiness. The proposed MILES framework addresses this gap by incorporating bed mobility, transfers, ambulation, and functional independence into a structured, mobility-centered assessment. It provides a conceptual foundation for future research on multidisciplinary discharge planning across acute trauma care and rehabilitation. Successful recovery in older adults should encompass survival, fracture healing, mobility, independence, participation, and quality of life. MILES complements existing trauma and frailty measures by emphasizing functional recovery. Further research is needed to establish its validity, reliability, predictive performance, and clinical utility before implementation in discharge decision-making.

title: A multicenter clinical study evaluating the efficacy of middle meningeal artery embolization combined with minimally invasive burr-hole drainage in the management of acute epidural hematoma
abstract: Background Acute epidural hematoma (AEDH) is a common and life-threatening condition following traumatic brain injury. Although conventional craniotomy provides definitive treatment, it is associated with substantial surgical trauma. Burr-hole drainage alone is insufficient to achieve effective control of arterial bleeding. Middle meningeal artery (MMA) embolization, a minimally invasive endovascular technique, enables direct occlusion of the bleeding source and may complement burr-hole drainage through a synergistic mechanism. However, multicenter, large-scale studies investigating this combined treatment strategy remain lacking. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on the clinical data of 135 patients with AEDH who were admitted to Shandong Medical and Pharmaceutical University Hospital, Dongying City People Hospital, and Binzhou City Central Hospital between January 2022 and June 2025. Among them, 39 patients underwent middle meningeal artery embolization combined with minimally invasive burr-hole drainage for hematoma evacuation, while the remaining 96 patients received craniotomy for hematoma removal. The 39 patients treated with embolization were assigned to the experimental group, and the other 96 patients served as the control group. The primary outcome measures included baseline patient characteristics, operative duration, intraoperative blood loss, postoperative complications, and Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) scores at admission and discharge. These parameters were compared between the two groups. Results A total of 135 patients were included in the study, comprising 39 patients who underwent middle meningeal artery embolization combined with minimally invasive burr-hole drainage in the minimally invasive surgery group and 96 patients who underwent conventional craniotomy hematoma evacuation in the craniotomy group. Compared with the craniotomy group, the minimally invasive surgery group exhibited a higher postoperative hematoma residual rate and a longer mean drainage duration. Nevertheless, the minimally invasive surgery group had a shorter operative time and lower intraoperative blood loss than the craniotomy group. The postoperative reoperation rate was lower in the minimally invasive surgery group, while the incidence of postoperative complications and length of postoperative hospital stay were significantly reduced compared with those in the craniotomy group. Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) scores at discharge were significantly improved compared with baseline values at admission in both groups, with no statistically significant difference observed between the two groups. Additionally, patients in the minimally invasive surgery group required fewer blood transfusions and received a lower transfusion volume than those in the craniotomy group. Conclusion Using middle meningeal artery embolization combined with minimally invasive burr hole drainage to treat acute epidural hematoma can achieve good clinical outcomes. This technique is a feasible treatment option for acute epidural hematomas caused by middle meningeal artery bleeding.

title: Predicting 1‑Year Recurrence Risk in First‑Ever Ischemic Stroke: A Machine Learning Approach Using Routine Clinical Data
abstract: We developed and internally validated machine-learning models to predict 1-year recurrence after first-ever ischemic stroke using routinely available clinical data. This retrospective single-center cohort included patients treated between 2022 and 2024. Predictors were selected using univariate analysis, LASSO regression, and Boruta, and seven machine-learning models were compared with the ESRS and SPI-II scores. Among 1,868 patients, 136 (7.28%) experienced recurrence within 1 year. Nine predictors were retained: age, hyperlipidemia, admission NIHSS score, discharge mRS score, hypertension, diabetes, smoking, LDL-C, and homocysteine. XGBoost showed strong discrimination in the test set (AUC 0.860, 95% CI 0.786–0.933) and significantly outperformed most models, particularly ESRS and SPI-II (both P < 0.001), whereas differences from LightGBM and random forest were not significant. XGBoost also showed favorable calibration and clinical net benefit. SHAP analysis identified admission NIHSS as the most influential predictor. An R Shiny application was developed for individualized risk estimation. These findings suggest that routinely available clinical variables combined with machine learning may support recurrence risk stratification, although external validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Case Report: A novel surgical drainage bag-derived plastic sheet-assisted keratoprosthesis implantation technique: a retrospective case series
abstract: Objective Corneal blindness is one of the important contributors to the burden of global blindness. This report describes a novel surgical drainage bag-derived plastic sheet (PS)-assisted technique for collar-button keratoprosthesis (CbKpro) implantation, which is intended to provide temporary mechanical protection during the open-sky phase of surgery. This retrospective series was designed primarily to evaluate the technical feasibility of the procedure, and the technique is hypothesized to reduce procedure-related risks in high-risk eyes with end-stage corneal blindness. Methods Six eyes of five patients with end-stage corneal blindness underwent PS-assisted CbKpro implantation and were retrospectively reviewed. The mean follow-up duration was 15.67 ± 10.69 months (range, 6–36 months). The primary outcome was the occurrence of suprachoroidal hemorrhage (SCH) and intraocular content extrusion. Secondary outcomes included the intraoperative technical performance of the PS, individual preoperative and postoperative best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), intraocular pressure (IOP), postoperative complications and additional surgical procedures. Results The PS-assisted technique provided a transparent, low-cost temporary barrier across the graft bed during CbKpro implantation and preserved intraoperative visualization in all six eyes. No intraoperative SCH or intraocular content extrusion was observed. Postoperative BCVA improved in all eyes, from light perception (LP) or hand motion (HM) preoperatively to counting fingers (CF) or functional acuity ranging from 3/20 to 18/20 at the last follow-up. One eye (Case 2) required an additional vitrectomy on postoperative day 3 for retained lens cortex; no other adverse event requiring additional surgery was recorded. No retroprosthetic membrane (RPM) formation or device extrusion requiring additional surgery was observed during follow-up. Conclusion In this small retrospective case series, PS-assisted CbKpro implantation was technically feasible and was not associated with intraoperative SCH or intraocular content extrusion. Because these findings derive from only six eyes without a control group and SCH has a low baseline incidence, they should be interpreted as evidence of feasibility rather than of a reduction in the risk of intraoperative complications. Larger prospective controlled studies with longer follow-up are required to confirm safety and reproducibility.

title: Cryptococcal meningitis complicated by hydrocephalus in an apparently immunocompetent farmer: a case report
abstract: Cryptococcal meningoencephalitis is an opportunistic fungal infection that predominantly affects immunocompromised individuals. However, an increasing number of cases have been reported in apparently immunocompetent hosts, posing important diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. We report the case of a 64-year-old previously healthy farmer living in a rural area who presented with a 10-day history of severe diffuse headache, fever, photophobia, and phonophobia followed by horizontal binocular diplopia. Neurological examination revealed neck stiffness and bilateral grade IV papilledema. Brain MRI demonstrated early active tetraventricular hydrocephalus with transependymal cerebrospinal fluid resorption. CSF analysis showed lymphocytic meningitis with elevated protein levels, profound hypoglycorrhachia, and positive multiplex PCR, India ink staining, culture for Cryptococcus neoformans. Despite prompt induction therapy with liposomal amphotericin B plus fluconazole, progressive hydrocephalus developed, requiring neuronavigation-guided external ventricular drainage. An extensive immunological workup, including repeated HIV testing and lymphocyte subset analysis, excluded persistent immunodeficiency, with the initial transient lymphopenia resolving during treatment. The patient improved clinically, cerebrospinal fluid cultures became sterile, and he was discharged on oral fluconazole. Unexpectedly, he died at home from an undetermined cause. This case highlights the potential severity and complexity of cryptococcal meningoencephalitis, even in apparently immunocompetent patients, despite appropriate and aggressive management. Early recognition and prompt treatment of intracranial complications are essential, while a thorough evaluation for underlying immunodeficiency should always be undertaken. Close and prolonged clinical monitoring remains warranted throughout the disease course.

title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor–associated neuromuscular–cardiac overlap toxicity in thoracic malignancies: early recognition and organ-directed management in a three-case series
abstract: Background Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-associated myasthenia gravis (MG), myositis, and myocarditis may overlap and rapidly cause respiratory or cardiac failure. In thoracic malignancies, early ptosis and dyspnea may be mistaken for tumor progression, infection, pneumonitis, or heart failure. Methods We retrospectively reviewed three patients with thoracic malignancies who developed suspected ICI-associated neuromuscular–cardiac toxicity after PD-1 inhibitor therapy at a single center. Clinical manifestations, neuromuscular and cardiac investigations, respiratory involvement, treatment, and outcomes were descriptively analyzed. Results All three patients developed unilateral ptosis with acetylcholine receptor antibody positivity and cardiac biomarker elevation 20–50 days after initial PD-1 inhibitor exposure. Case 1 progressed to severe hypercapnic ventilatory failure requiring noninvasive ventilation, IVIG, and subsequent centrifugal plasma exchange (PLEX); Case 2 developed high-risk conduction-system disease requiring temporary pacing and was treated with expedited PLEX without preceding IVIG to target the neuromuscular component; and Case 3 had mild ocular manifestations with CK and troponin elevation despite negative neostigmine and repetitive nerve stimulation testing. Across successive cases, management evolved from reactive rescue in Case 1 to earlier multisystem assessment and organ-directed intervention in Cases 2 and 3. All three patients survived the acute immune-toxicity episode and were discharged. Conclusions New-onset ptosis after ICI exposure should prompt immediate parallel neuromuscular, cardiac, and respiratory assessment. Management should be matched to the dominant organ threat, with severity-guided pulse-dose corticosteroids, IVIG or plasma exchange for severe or rapidly progressive neuromuscular involvement, and timely cardiac or ventilatory support when indicated.

title: Reframing mental health task-sharing in Somalia: from specialist scarcity to supervised primary care integration
abstract: Somalia faces a substantial and largely unmet mental health burden shaped by protracted conflict, recurrent humanitarian crises, internal displacement, and poverty. Severe specialist scarcity, weak primary care mental health capacity, inconsistent psychotropic medicine availability, and limited supervision structures mean that a specialist-dependent model alone is unlikely to close the treatment gap within a realistic planning horizon. This Perspective argues that Somalia should reconceptualise task-sharing not as an informal substitute for scarce specialists, but as a supervised, quality-assured, primary-care-integrated strategy for expanding safe and accessible mental health care. Drawing on Somalia-specific evidence and implementation evidence from comparable low-resource settings, we identify core system requirements: competency-based mhGAP training; district-level specialist supervision; functioning referral pathways; reliable essential medicines; psychosocial support; community engagement; routine monitoring; and human rights safeguards. Task-sharing without these components risks becoming an unsafe service substitution rather than a genuine system strengthening. Specialists remain indispensable for supervision, complex case management, training and clinical governance. Somalia-specific implementation research should accompany phased implementation and scale-up. We propose that supervised, quality-assured task-sharing could provide a primary-care pathway for developing and evaluating more accessible mental health services in Somalia.

title: Preoperative risk stratification for fear of cancer recurrence trajectories in thyroid cancer survivors: a prospective latent class growth analysis
abstract: Objective This prospective cohort study aimed to delineate distinct Fear of Cancer Recurrence (FCR) trajectories over the first year after surgery and to identify baseline demographic, clinical, and psychosocial factors associated with trajectory class membership. Methods Consecutive patients scheduled for initial surgery for Papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) in China (N = 458), were invited to participate. FCR was assessed using the 42-item Chinese version of the Fear of Cancer Recurrence Inventory (FCRI-CV) at four time points: admission (T1, preoperative baseline), and 1, 6, and 12 months post-discharge (T2–T4). Social support was measured with the Social Support Rating Scale, and anxiety and depressive symptoms were evaluated using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale at T1. Latent class growth analysis (LCGA) was employed to identify trajectory classes, and multinomial logistic regression was used to examine which baseline factors were associated with membership in the higher-fear classes. Results LCGA revealed a three-class model with high classification certainty (entropy = 0.967). The Low-Fear Declining class (30.2%) exhibited low initial FCR followed by a linear decline (intercept = 70.86, slope = -1.94). The Moderate-Fear Declining class (45.2%) began at an intermediate FCR level with a similar decline (intercept = 90.09, slope = -1.88). The High-Fear Declining class (24.5%) remained the highest-FCR trajectory throughout follow-up despite a significant linear decline (intercept = 108.69, slope = -1.68).
